short_description.id: Huān Dōu adalah penguasa Miao dalam tradisi Tiongkok kuno yang kemudian juga ditafsirkan sebagai makhluk mitologis.
short_description.en: Huān Dōu is a Miao ruler in ancient Chinese tradition, later also interpreted as a mythical being.

long_description.id: Huān Dōu adalah penguasa Miao dalam tradisi Tiongkok kuno yang kemudian juga ditafsirkan sebagai makhluk mitologis. Tradisi menyebut pengasingannya sebagai salah satu Empat Penjahat pada masa Shun. Sebuah teks klasik menyebut Huandou dibuang ke Gunung Chong bersama tiga hukuman lain, dan setelah itu seluruh negeri tunduk. Tidak ada bukti sezaman tentang keberadaannya karena ia hanya dikenal dari teks Tiongkok awal yang diwariskan.
long_description.en: Huān Dōu is a Miao ruler in ancient Chinese tradition, later also interpreted as a mythical being. Tradition describes his exile as one of the Four Criminals under Shun. A classical text says Huandou was banished to Mount Chong together with three other punishments, after which the whole realm submitted. There is no contemporary evidence of his existence, since he is known only from transmitted early Chinese texts.

long_description.id: Nama Huandou dan Huantou mempunyai beberapa varian aksara. Zhang Shoujie menyamakannya dengan Hundun, sedangkan Lüshi Chunqiu menggunakannya sebagai nama negeri. Kisah menyebut Huandou mengusulkan Gonggong untuk menangani banjir, tetapi Yao menolaknya karena menilainya pemimpin yang membangkang dan cacat. Teks klasik juga mencatat Huandou berbicara untuk Gonggong, dan sang kaisar menolak dengan menyebut Gonggong pandai bicara tetapi berbuat sebaliknya.
long_description.en: The names Huandou and Huantou have several written variants. Zhang Shoujie equates him with Hundun, while the Lüshi Chunqiu uses it as a state's name. The tale describes Huandou recommending Gonggong for flood control, but Yao rejected him, judging him a rebellious and flawed leader. A classical text also records Huandou speaking in favor of Gonggong, and the emperor refusing by saying Gonggong speaks smoothly but acts contrary.

long_description.id: Serbuan Yu membuat Huandou mundur ke Gunung Chong, dan pada serbuan kedua Yu Agung ia akhirnya dikalahkan sehingga Sanmiao hancur. Classic of Mountains and Seas mencatat Huandou sebagai keturunan Zhuanxu, sedangkan catatan lain dari teks yang sama menyebutnya cucu Gun. Teks itu juga memitoskan Huandou sebagai lelaki berparuh burung dan bersayap yang memakan ikan dari laut, dan sebuah teks klasik melukiskan penduduk negeri Huantou berwajah manusia, bersayap, dan berparuh burung. Orang Miao masa kini mengakui Huandou bersama Chi You sebagai leluhur mereka.
long_description.en: The invasion by Yu led Huandou to retreat to Mount Chong, and in a second invasion by Yu the Great he was finally defeated, destroying the Sanmiao. In the Classic of Mountains and Seas, Huandou is traced to Zhuanxu in one line of descent and to Gun, Earl of Chong, as grandfather in another. The text also mythologises Huandou as a bird-beaked, winged man who eats fish from the sea, and a classical text depicts the people of the Huantou country as human-faced, winged, and bird-beaked. The modern Miao people claim Huandou, along with Chi You, as their progenitor.

text.en: In tales set in the Heian period

short_description.id: Ibaraki-dōji adalah oni dalam kisah zaman Heian, pengikut terpenting Shuten-dōji yang berbasis di Gunung Ōe dan pernah mengamuk di Kyoto. Ia terkenal lewat kisah lengannya yang ditebas Watanabe no Tsuna.
short_description.en: Ibaraki-dōji is an oni of Heian-period tales, the most important servant of Shuten-dōji, based on Mount Ōe and once on a rampage in Kyoto. He is famed for the tale of his arm cut off by Watanabe no Tsuna.

long_description.id: Ibaraki-dōji (茨木童子) adalah oni dalam kisah yang berlatar zaman Heian. Cerita menempatkannya di Gunung Ōe dan menyebut ia pernah mengamuk di Kyoto. Ia disebut pengikut terpenting Shuten-dōji, dan satu kisah menggambarkannya sebagai raksasa menakutkan yang sudah bergigi sejak lahir.
long_description.en: Ibaraki-dōji (茨木童子) is an oni in tales set in the Heian period. The stories place him on Mount Ōe and say he once went on a rampage in Kyoto. He is named the most important servant of Shuten-dōji, and one account describes a fearsome giant born with teeth.

long_description.id: Kelompok Shuten-dōji dihancurkan oleh Minamoto no Yorimitsu dan empat pengikutnya, tetapi Ibaraki-dōji berhasil lolos. Kisah paling terkenal tentangnya menyangkut Watanabe no Tsuna: Tsuna menebas lengan oni itu, dan oni itu kemudian menyamar untuk merebut lengannya kembali. Dalam satu versi ia menyamar sebagai gadis lalu berubah menjadi oni dan membawa Tsuna terbang; dalam versi lain ia menyamar sebagai ibu susu Tsuna.
long_description.en: The Shuten-dōji gang was destroyed by Minamoto no Yorimitsu and his four vassals, but Ibaraki-dōji managed to escape. The best-known tale concerns Watanabe no Tsuna: Tsuna cuts off the oni's arm, and the oni later disguises itself to take the arm back. In one version it appears as a girl, turns into an oni and flies off with Tsuna; in another it disguises itself as Tsuna's wet nurse.

long_description.id: Jenis kelamin Ibaraki-dōji tidak jelas: kebanyakan kisah menggambarkannya sebagai kijo (oni perempuan), tetapi ada kisah yang menyebutnya laki-laki. Tempat lahirnya juga diperselisihkan antara Provinsi Settsu dan Echigo. Setelah kisah lengannya, keberadaannya tidak diketahui, meski penduduk kadang mengaku melihatnya bersama semacam kenakalan.
long_description.en: Ibaraki-dōji's gender is unclear: most stories depict a kijo (female oni), but some give a male. His birthplace is also disputed between Settsu and Echigo provinces. After the tale of the arm his whereabouts are unknown, though villagers sometimes claimed to see him, always with some mischief.

literal_meaning.id: Dua sumber berbeda: "anak pohon berduri" (Yokai.com), atau "Ibaraki" yang mungkin merujuk pada Ibaraki di Osaka dengan "dōji" berarti "anak".
literal_meaning.en: Two sources differ: "thorn tree child" (Yokai.com), or "Ibaraki" possibly referring to Ibaraki, Osaka with "dōji" meaning "child".

description.id: Dalam kisah-kisah itu ia menyamar sebagai gadis cantik lalu berubah kembali menjadi oni, atau menyamar sebagai ibu susu Watanabe no Tsuna.
description.en: In the tales he appears as a beautiful girl and then turns back into an oni, or disguises himself as Watanabe no Tsuna's wet nurse.

claims.quote: Ibaraki-dōji (茨木童子 or 茨城童子 "Ibaraki child") is an oni (demon or ogre) featured in tales of the Heian period.

statement.id: Ibaraki-dōji adalah oni dalam kisah yang berlatar zaman Heian.
statement.en: Ibaraki-dōji is an oni in tales set in the Heian period.

claims.quote: In the tales, Ibaraki-dōji is based on Mount Ōe, and once went on a rampage in Kyoto.

statement.id: Cerita-cerita menempatkan oni ini di Gunung Ōe dan Kyoto.
statement.en: Stories place the oni on Mount Ōe and in Kyoto.

claims.quote: Ibaraki-dōji was the most important servant of Shuten-dōji.

statement.id: Ibaraki-dōji digambarkan sebagai pengikut utama Shuten-dōji.
statement.en: Ibaraki-dōji is portrayed as a leading servant of Shuten-dōji.

claims.quote: Ibaraki-dōji had teeth since birth, and was feared for being a giant.

statement.id: Satu kisah menggambarkannya sebagai raksasa menakutkan yang sudah bergigi sejak lahir.
statement.en: One account describes a fearsome giant born with teeth.

claims.quote: Translation: a nickname meaning “thorn tree child”

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nama itu adalah julukan yang berarti "anak pohon berduri".
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, the name is a nickname meaning "thorn tree child".

claims.quote: The "Ibaraki" in his name may refer to Ibaraki, Osaka; "dōji" means "child", but in this context is a demon offspring.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Inggris, "Ibaraki" dalam namanya mungkin merujuk pada Ibaraki di Osaka; "dōji" berarti "anak", tetapi di sini bermakna keturunan iblis.
statement.en: According to the English article, the "Ibaraki" in his name may refer to Ibaraki, Osaka; "dōji" means "child", but here it denotes a demon offspring.

claims.quote: Most stories and illustrations depict Ibaraki dōji as a kijo, or a female oni; yet there are other stories which refer to Shuten dōji’s deputy as a male.

statement.id: Kebanyakan kisah dan ilustrasi menggambarkan Ibaraki-dōji sebagai kijo (oni perempuan), tetapi ada kisah lain yang menyebut wakil Shuten-dōji itu laki-laki.
statement.en: Most stories and illustrations depict Ibaraki-dōji as a kijo (a female oni), but other stories refer to Shuten-dōji's deputy as male.

claims.quote: Their gender is ambiguous, in some stories Ibaraki is a kijo (female oni), and in others a male. The female version is theorized to be Shuten-dōji’s lover, son, or his son's lover.

statement.id: Jenis kelaminnya tidak jelas: dalam beberapa kisah ia kijo (oni perempuan), dalam kisah lain laki-laki; versi perempuan diduga kekasih Shuten-dōji, anaknya, atau kekasih anaknya.
statement.en: Their gender is ambiguous: in some stories a kijo (female oni), in others male; the female version is theorized to be Shuten-dōji's lover, son, or his son's lover.

claims.quote: The gang ran amok in the capital, kidnapping families’ girls among other things, but they were destroyed by Minamoto no Yorimitsu and his four vassals, the Four Guardian Kings. However, Ibaraki-dōji was able to escape.

statement.id: Kelompok Shuten-dōji mengamuk di ibu kota, antara lain menculik gadis-gadis dari berbagai keluarga, tetapi dihancurkan oleh Minamoto no Yorimitsu dan empat pengikutnya, Empat Raja Penjaga; Ibaraki-dōji berhasil lolos.
statement.en: The Shuten-dōji gang ran amok in the capital, among other things kidnapping families' girls, but was destroyed by Minamoto no Yorimitsu and his four vassals, the Four Guardian Kings; Ibaraki-dōji managed to escape.

claims.quote: A young beautiful girl was on the road, worried, so Watanabe no Tsuna made her ride on a horse, but the girl suddenly transformed into an oni, and grasped Tsuna’s hair, flew in the air, and took him to Mount Atago. Tsuna, not panicked at all, cut off the oni's arm, averting disaster.

statement.id: Dalam satu versi, seorang gadis cantik yang tampak cemas dinaikkan ke kuda oleh Watanabe no Tsuna, lalu tiba-tiba berubah menjadi oni, mencengkeram rambut Tsuna, terbang, dan membawanya ke Gunung Atago; Tsuna menebas lengan oni itu dan lolos.
statement.en: In one version, a beautiful, worried-looking girl is put on a horse by Watanabe no Tsuna, suddenly turns into an oni, grasps Tsuna's hair, flies up and carries him toward Mount Atago; Tsuna cuts off the oni's arm and escapes.

claims.quote: Several days after that, Ibaraki-dōji tried to invade Tsuna's estate using the remaining arm, but due to the power of a Humane King Sutra and a talisman, Ibaraki-dōji was not able to enter.

statement.id: Beberapa hari kemudian Ibaraki-dōji berusaha menyusup ke kediaman Tsuna, tetapi tak bisa masuk karena kekuatan Sutra Raja Penyayang dan sebuah jimat.
statement.en: Several days later Ibaraki-dōji tried to break into Tsuna's estate but could not enter because of the power of a Humane King Sutra and a talisman.

claims.quote: Tsuna wasted no time, and swung his great katana around, severing the arm of an enormous demon: it was Ibaraki dōji, coming to avenge the murder of Shuten dōji. The injured demon ran away, leaving her arm behind, and Rashōmon was no longer haunted.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, di gerbang Rashōmon Tsuna menebas lengan iblis raksasa yang ternyata Ibaraki-dōji, yang datang membalas kematian Shuten-dōji; ia kabur meninggalkan lengannya dan Rashōmon tak lagi angker.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, at the Rashōmon gate Tsuna severed the arm of an enormous demon who was Ibaraki-dōji, come to avenge Shuten-dōji's death; she fled leaving her arm behind and Rashōmon was no longer haunted.

claims.quote: Ibaraki dōji later returned to Rashōmon, looking for her arm. She disguised herself as Watanabe no Tsuna’s wetnurse, and was able to steal back her severed arm and flee.

statement.id: Ibaraki-dōji kemudian kembali ke Rashōmon mencari lengannya; ia menyamar sebagai ibu susu Watanabe no Tsuna, berhasil mencuri kembali lengan yang terpotong itu, lalu kabur.
statement.en: Ibaraki-dōji later returned to Rashōmon looking for her arm; she disguised herself as Watanabe no Tsuna's wet nurse, managed to steal back the severed arm, and fled.

claims.quote: What is known is that Ibaraki dōji was a wholly terrible and fearsome monster, bent of wreaking as much havoc in the human world as possible.

statement.id: Yokai.com menggambarkan Ibaraki-dōji sebagai monster yang sepenuhnya mengerikan, bertekad membuat kekacauan sebanyak mungkin di dunia manusia.
statement.en: Yokai.com describes Ibaraki-dōji as a wholly terrible and fearsome monster, bent on wreaking as much havoc in the human world as possible.

claims.quote: As for the birthplace, there are theories that it may be Settsu Province (Mio, Ibaraki, Osaka, and Tomatsu, Amagasaki, Hyōgo) or Echigo Province (Niigata, formerly Tochio, now a settlement in Karuizawa, Nagano).

statement.id: Tentang tempat lahirnya, ada teori yang menyebut Provinsi Settsu (antara lain Mio di Ibaraki, Osaka, dan Tomatsu di Amagasaki, Hyōgo) atau Provinsi Echigo (Niigata).
statement.en: As for his birthplace, theories name Settsu Province (including Mio in Ibaraki, Osaka, and Tomatsu in Amagasaki, Hyōgo) or Echigo Province (Niigata).

claims.quote: After that, her whereabouts were never known again, though for many years after, occasionally in some town or another, villagers would claim that they had seen Ibaraki dōji coming or going, always in connection with some kind of mischief.

statement.id: Setelah itu keberadaannya tak pernah diketahui lagi, tetapi selama bertahun-tahun penduduk di berbagai kota sesekali mengaku melihat Ibaraki-dōji datang atau pergi, selalu bersama semacam kenakalan.
statement.en: After that her whereabouts were never known again, though for many years villagers in one town or another occasionally claimed to have seen Ibaraki-dōji coming or going, always connected with some mischief.

short_description.id: Iemisch adalah kriptid dari Patagonia dekat Danau Colhué; digambarkan bersifat nokturnal dan sangat kuat sehingga dapat menyeret kuda ke dasar air, tetapi para peneliti menduganya berang-berang atau macan yang belum dikenali.
short_description.en: The Iemisch is a cryptid from Patagonia near Lake Colhué, described as nocturnal and so strong it can drag horses to the bottom of the water, though researchers suggested it was an unrecognised otter or jaguar.

long_description.id: Iemisch (juga disebut Iemisch Listai) adalah kriptid dugaan dari Patagonia, khususnya di pegunungan dekat kawasan Danau Colhué. Pertama dicatat oleh Florentino Ameghino pada 1897, dan kajian lengkapnya terbit dalam buku On the Track of Unknown Animals tahun 1955. Ejaan lain dari para pencatat awal mencakup Chimchimen, Jémechim, Yem'chen, Jemisch, dan Hymché.
long_description.en: Reputed to dwell in the Patagonian mountains around Lake Colhué, the Iemisch (or Iemisch Listai) is a purported cryptid. Florentino Ameghino first recorded it in 1897, and the 1955 book On the Track of Unknown Animals gave it a complete study. Early recorders also wrote the name Chimchimen, Jémechim, Yem'chen, Jemisch and Hymché.

long_description.id: Hewan itu bersifat nokturnal dan konon begitu kuat sehingga dapat mencengkeram kuda dengan cakarnya dan menyeretnya ke dasar air. Menurut deskripsi dalam surat asli, kepalanya pendek, bertaring besar, tanpa telinga luar, berkaki pendek plantigrad dengan tiga jari depan dan empat belakang berselaput renang dan bercakar kuat, serta berekor panjang, pipih, dan dapat menggenggam. Ia konon bergerak secepat di darat seperti di air dan menjerit "soul-wrenching".
long_description.en: It keeps nocturnal habits and is reportedly strong enough to grab horses in its claws and haul them to the bottom of a lake or river. The original letter describes a short head, large canine teeth and no outer ears; short, flat-footed limbs with three toes in front and four behind, webbed for swimming and tipped with formidable claws; and a long, flat tail able to grip. Accounts say it is as fast on land as in water and gives a "soul-wrenching scream".

long_description.id: Robert Lehmann-Nitsche mengaku memiliki contoh kulit iemisch dari seorang peternak, dengan keping tulang kecil tertanam di kulit yang melindunginya dari mata panah. Dalam kajiannya, ia menulis bahwa kata Jemisch kemungkinan besar berarti berang-berang (Lutra felina) dan bahwa kisah hewan buas dalam mitos sebagian besar dapat merujuk pada macan. Ia dan Santiago Roth menyimpulkan bahwa iemisch tentulah sejenis berang-berang yang belum dikenal.
long_description.en: Robert Lehmann-Nitsche claimed to have a sample of iemisch skin from a rancher, with small bone plates embedded in it that protected the creature from arrowheads. In his study he wrote that the word Jemisch most probably means the otter (Lutra felina) and that tales of a fierce animal in the myths mostly may refer to the jaguar. He and Santiago Roth concluded it must be an unknown type of otter.

long_description.id: Paleontolog John Bell Hatcher mencatat bahwa walau lama bersama penduduk asli Patagonia ia tak pernah mendengar makhluk semacam itu, dan para sarjana kemudian meragukan penelitian Heuvelmans karena kata 'Iemisch' tidak dikaitkan dengan bahasa mana pun yang dituturkan di Patagonia. Tournouer, menurut Lehmann-Nitsche, mengaku melihat neomylodon yang misterius hidup di air, dan pemandunya menyebutnya Hymché.
long_description.en: The paleontologist John Bell Hatcher observed that he had never encountered such a creature even after comparable time among Patagonian natives, and later scholars questioned Heuvelmans's work because 'Iemisch' belongs to no language spoken in Patagonia. Lehmann-Nitsche reports that Tournouer claimed to have seen the mysterious neomylodon alive in the water, with his guide naming it Hymché.

statement.en: Lehmann-Nitsche and Santiago Roth later published more iemisch tales, concluding it must be an unknown type of otter; paleontologist John Bell Hatcher noted that despite spending as much time with Patagonian natives he had never heard of such a creature.

claims.quote: Later scholars also cast doubt on research by Heuvelmans, noting that the word 'Iemisch' isn't associated with any language spoken in Patagonia.

statement.id: Para sarjana kemudian meragukan penelitian Heuvelmans, mencatat bahwa kata 'Iemisch' tidak dikaitkan dengan bahasa mana pun yang dituturkan di Patagonia.
statement.en: Later scholars also cast doubt on Heuvelmans's research, noting that the word 'Iemisch' is not associated with any language spoken in Patagonia.

claims.quote: Los mitos (capítulo III), leyendas y cuentos de los indios en que se habla de un animal feroz, pueden referirse en su mayoría al tigre

statement.id: Lehmann-Nitsche berpendapat bahwa mitos, legenda, dan cerita orang Indian tentang hewan buas sebagian besar dapat merujuk pada macan (tigre).
statement.en: Lehmann-Nitsche argues that the Indians' myths, legends and tales of a fierce animal mostly may refer to the jaguar (tigre).

claims.quote: « Chimchimen », de la Cruz y Gay. «Jémechim», Lista. « Yem'chen», Moreno. «Jemisch», Carlos Ameghino. « Hymché », Tournouer.

statement.id: Lehmann-Nitsche mendaftar ejaan lain nama ini dari para pencatat sebelumnya: Chimchimen (Febres, de la Cruz dan Gay), Jémechim (Lista), Yem'chen (Moreno), Jemisch (Carlos Ameghino), dan Hymché (Tournouer).
statement.en: Lehmann-Nitsche lists other spellings of the name from earlier recorders: Chimchimen (de la Cruz and Gay), Jémechim (Lista), Yem'chen (Moreno), Jemisch (Carlos Ameghino) and Hymché (Tournouer).

claims.quote: haber visto en la Patagonia al neomylodon enigmático, vivo en el agua. El guía lo llamó Hymché.

statement.id: Lehmann-Nitsche mencatat bahwa Tournouer mengaku melihat neomylodon yang misterius hidup di air di Patagonia, dan pemandunya menyebutnya Hymché.
statement.en: Lehmann-Nitsche records that Tournouer claimed to have seen the enigmatic neomylodon living in the water in Patagonia, and his guide called it Hymché.

summary.en: Lehmann-Nitsche and Roth: it must be an unknown type of otter; the word Jemisch most probably means the otter.

text.en: Sightings reported since well before Alaska became a state

short_description.id: Iliamna Lake Monster adalah makhluk air tak dikenal dalam cerita warga sekitar Iliamna Lake [iliamna-lake-monster-c01].
short_description.en: The Iliamna Lake Monster is an unknown aquatic creature in the stories of Iliamna Lake residents [iliamna-lake-monster-c01].

long_description.id: Warga sekitar Iliamna Lake punya banyak cerita tentang Iliamna Lake Monster, makhluk air tak dikenal [iliamna-lake-monster-c01]. Nama Iliamna sendiri konon nama ikan hitam besar mitos yang melubangi perahu penduduk yang jahat [iliamna-lake-monster-c02], dan berasal dari nama Dena'ina Nila Vena, "danau pulau" [iliamna-lake-monster-c05]. Danau itu terbesar di Alaska [iliamna-lake-monster-c06].
long_description.en: Iliamna Lake residents tell many stories of the Iliamna Lake Monster, an unknown aquatic creature [iliamna-lake-monster-c01]. The name Iliamna itself is said to be that of a mythical great blackfish that holes the boats of bad natives [iliamna-lake-monster-c02], and it derives from the Dena'ina name Nila Vena, "island's lake" [iliamna-lake-monster-c05]. The lake is the largest in Alaska [iliamna-lake-monster-c06].

long_description.id: Menurut laporan berita, penampakan makhluk raksasa mirip ikan dilaporkan sejak jauh sebelum Alaska menjadi negara bagian; kebanyakan saksi menyebutnya gelap, mirip hiu, dan panjang 10 sampai 20 kaki [iliamna-lake-monster-c09], sering lebih dari satu dan sedang berburu [iliamna-lake-monster-c10]. Dalam satu catatan, seekor makhluk sepanjang dan selebar perahu 18 kaki dengan mata sebesar bola sepak [iliamna-lake-monster-c12].
long_description.en: According to a news report, sightings of giant fish-like creatures have been reported since well before Alaska became a state; most witnesses call them dark, shark-like and 10 to 20 feet long [iliamna-lake-monster-c09], often more than one and hunting [iliamna-lake-monster-c10]. In one account, a creature was as long and wide as an 18-foot skiff with eyes the circumference of soccer balls [iliamna-lake-monster-c12].

long_description.id: Ada dugaan penampakan itu sturgeon putih [iliamna-lake-monster-c03], hiu tidur Pasifik [iliamna-lake-monster-c07], atau pike utara raksasa [iliamna-lake-monster-c14]; laporan berburu anjing laut dan memangsa salmon dinilai tidak cocok dengan sturgeon [iliamna-lake-monster-c11]. Sebuah surat kabar pernah menawarkan hadiah $100.000 untuk buktinya [iliamna-lake-monster-c04], tetapi belum ada bukti pasti diumumkan [iliamna-lake-monster-c13]. Penampakan baru dilaporkan pada 2017 [iliamna-lake-monster-c08], dan seorang pria merasa yakin setelah jangkarnya terseret [iliamna-lake-monster-c15].
long_description.en: Sightings have been suggested to be white sturgeon [iliamna-lake-monster-c03], Pacific sleeper shark [iliamna-lake-monster-c07] or giant northern pike [iliamna-lake-monster-c14]; reports of hunting seals and preying on salmon are said not to fit a sturgeon [iliamna-lake-monster-c11]. A newspaper once offered $100,000 for proof [iliamna-lake-monster-c04], but no definitive proof has been made public [iliamna-lake-monster-c13]. New sightings were reported in 2017 [iliamna-lake-monster-c08], and one man became convinced after his anchor was dragged [iliamna-lake-monster-c15].

claims.quote: Since well before Alaska became a state, there have been numerous reported sightings of giant fish-like creatures in the lake. There’s some variation in descriptions, but most witnesses say the creatures are dark colored, shark-like in appearance and between 10 and 20-feet long.

claims.quote: Often there’s more than one together and frequently, the creatures are hunting.

statement.id: Menurut laporan berita itu, sering ada lebih dari satu makhluk bersama-sama dan sering kali makhluk-makhluk itu sedang berburu.

claims.quote: However, reports of the creatures’ predatory behavior — herding seals into shallows to hunt them and preying upon schools of sockeye salmon — don’t sound like a sturgeon.

statement.en: According to the news report, reports of the creatures' predatory behavior, herding seals into shallows to hunt them and preying upon schools of sockeye salmon, do not sound like a sturgeon.

statement.en: In one account recorded in the news report, one creature was the length and width of the hunters' 18-foot skiff with eyes the circumference of soccer balls, and the creatures looked like giant northern pike.

claims.quote: In 1980, the Anchorage Daily News offered a $100,000 reward during a five-month period to anyone who presented clear evidence of the monsters. No definitive proof has been made public, though there have been sightings reported most years since.

statement.id: Pada 1980 Anchorage Daily News menawarkan hadiah $100.000 selama lima bulan bagi siapa pun yang menunjukkan bukti jelas; belum ada bukti pasti diumumkan, meski penampakan dilaporkan hampir setiap tahun sejak itu.

claims.quote: For years, Wright theorized that the monsters might be Pacific sleeper sharks that adapted to living in freshwater. Now, he’s wondering if they might be a tiny population of gargantuan northern pike. Others have theorized they’re giant sturgeon.

statement.en: For years Wright theorized the monsters might be Pacific sleeper sharks adapted to freshwater; now he wonders if they might be a tiny population of gargantuan northern pike; others have theorized giant sturgeon.

claims.quote: In 2017, after several summers with no action, Stigar had an experience that convinced him the monsters were real. On that day he went to check his longline set and was surprised to see that his 38-pound anchor had been dragged 50 yards.

short_description.id: İmrə adalah jin musim semi dalam budaya rakyat Turk dan Altai yang dipercaya membentuk Cemre, kehangatan yang jatuh berturut-turut ke udara, air, dan tanah pada awal musim semi.
short_description.en: İmrə is the spring jinn of Turkic and Altai folk culture, believed to make up the Cemre, the warmth that falls in turn into the air, water and earth at the start of spring.

long_description.id: İmrə, yang juga disebut İmere, Əmrə, Emire, atau Emre, adalah jin musim semi dalam budaya rakyat dan mitologi Turk dan Altai. Ia dipercaya membentuk Cemre, yaitu kenaikan panas pada awal musim semi yang muncul berselang tujuh hari: mula-mula di udara, lalu di air dan tanah. Menurut sumber, Cemre pertama jatuh ke udara pada 20 Februari.
long_description.en: İmrə, also called İmere, Əmrə, Emire or Emre, is the spring jinn of Turkic and Altai folk culture and mythology. It is believed to make up the Cemre, the rise in warmth at the start of spring that comes at seven-day intervals: first in the air, then in water and earth. According to the source, the first Cemre falls into the air on 20 February.

long_description.id: Pada musim semi İmrə muncul dan naik ke langit sambil memancarkan cahaya yang bergetar. Setelah itu ia jatuh ke atas es dan mencairkannya, lalu masuk ke dalam tanah, sehingga uap naik dari tanah yang sudah hangat. Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Anadolu, Cemre digambarkan sebagai bara api legendaris yang jatuh ke udara, air, dan tanah serta menghangatkannya; sebuah ensiklopedia daring menyebutnya tiga bara yang dikirim oleh jin pada akhir musim dingin.
long_description.en: In spring İmrə appears and rises to the sky, giving off flickering lights. It then falls onto the ice and melts it, and enters the ground, so that steam rises from the warmed earth. In Anadolu folk belief the Cemre is pictured as a legendary ember that falls into the air, water and earth and warms them; an online encyclopedia calls them three embers sent by a genie at the end of winter.

long_description.id: İmrə melambangkan datangnya musim semi. Di kalangan orang Bulgar, makhluk ini dikenal sebagai Zemire, dan sumber kedua menganggap jin Zemire itu sebagai bentuk tertua konsep ini.
long_description.en: İmrə represents the coming of spring. Among the Bulgars it is known as Zemire, and the second source regards that jinn Zemire as the oldest form of the concept.

claims.quote: İmrə , Yaz başlanğıcında Cemreyi (yeddi gün ara ilə əvvəl hava, sonra su və torpaqda meydana gəldiyi sanılan istilik artımını) təşkil edən cin.

statement.id: İmrə adalah jin (cin) yang membentuk Cemre, yaitu kenaikan panas pada awal musim semi yang dipercaya muncul berselang tujuh hari, pertama di udara, lalu di air dan tanah.
statement.en: İmrə is the jinn (cin) that makes up the Cemre, the rise in warmth at the start of spring believed to arise at seven-day intervals, first in the air and then in water and earth.

claims.quote: Türk və altay xalq mədəniyyətində və mifologiyasında İmrə (İmere və ya Əmrə) yazda görünüb titrək işıqlar saçaraq göyə yüksəlir.

statement.id: Dalam budaya rakyat dan mitologi Turk dan Altai (Türk və altay), İmrə (İmere atau Əmrə) muncul pada musim semi dan naik ke langit sambil memancarkan cahaya yang bergetar.
statement.en: In Turkic and Altai (Türk və altay) folk culture and mythology, İmrə (İmere or Əmrə) appears in spring and rises to the sky, shedding flickering lights.

claims.quote: Sonra buzların üzərinə düşərək onları əridir. Oradan da yerə girər. Bundan sonra istilənmiş torpaqdan buxar yüksələr.

statement.id: Lalu ia jatuh ke atas es (buzların) dan mencairkannya, kemudian masuk ke tanah; setelah itu uap naik dari tanah yang telah hangat.
statement.en: Then it falls onto the ice (buzların) and melts it, and from there enters the ground; afterwards steam rises from the warmed earth.

claims.quote: İmrə baharın gəlişini təmsil edir. Bulqarlarda Zemire olaraq iştirak edər.

statement.id: İmrə melambangkan datangnya musim semi (baharın gəlişini); di kalangan orang Bulgar (Bulqarlarda) ia dikenal sebagai Zemire.
statement.en: İmrə represents the coming of spring (baharın gəlişini); among the Bulgars (Bulqarlarda) it appears as Zemire.

claims.quote: Anadolu Türkcəsində, Ərəbcədən gəlmə Cemre sözcüyünün əslində bu adın bənzətmə ilə dəyişmiş halı olduğu deyilə bilər.

statement.id: Dapat dikatakan bahwa kata Cemre dalam bahasa Turki Anadolu, yang berasal dari bahasa Arab (Ərəbcədən), sebenarnya adalah bentuk nama ini yang berubah karena kemiripan.
statement.en: It can be said that the word Cemre in Anadolu Turkish, which comes from Arabic (Ərəbcədən), is in fact a form of this name altered by analogy.

claims.quote: İlk Cemre 20 Fevralda havaya və yeddi gün ara ilə də suya və torpağa düşər.

statement.id: Cemre pertama jatuh ke udara pada 20 Februari (20 Fevralda), lalu dengan selang tujuh hari ke air dan ke tanah.
statement.en: The first Cemre falls into the air on 20 February (20 Fevralda), and at seven-day intervals into the water and the earth.

claims.quote: Eşdeğer: İMERE, EMİRE, EMRE Bahar Cinidir.

statement.id: Nama padanan İmre adalah İmere, Emire, dan Emre; ia adalah jin musim semi (bahar cini).
statement.en: Equivalent names of İmre are İmere, Emire and Emre; it is the spring jinn (bahar cini).

claims.quote: Bulgarlardaki Zemire adlı cinin bu kavramın en eski biçimi olduğu anlaşılmaktadır.

statement.id: Jin bernama Zemire di kalangan orang Bulgar (Bulgarlardaki) dipahami sebagai bentuk tertua konsep ini.
statement.en: The jinn called Zemire among the Bulgars (Bulgarlardaki) is understood to be the oldest form of this concept.

claims.quote: Anadolu halk inanışında Cemre doğal unsurlara temas ederek onların ısınmasını sağlayar efsânevî ateştir. Havaya, suya ve toprağa düşen kor parçasıdır.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Anadolu, Cemre adalah api legendaris (efsânevî ateş) yang menghangatkan unsur-unsur alam dengan menyentuhnya; ia adalah bara (kor) yang jatuh ke udara, air, dan tanah.
statement.en: In Anadolu folk belief the Cemre is a legendary fire (efsânevî ateş) that warms the natural elements by touching them; it is an ember (kor) falling into the air, the water and the earth.

claims.quote: Sözcük Arapça kökenlidir ve Camra/Camrah kelimesi bu dilde kor veyâ köz mânâsı taşır.

statement.id: Kata Cemre berasal dari bahasa Arab (Arapça); dalam bahasa itu Camra/Camrah berarti bara (kor, köz).
statement.en: The word Cemre is of Arabic (Arapça) origin; in that language Camra/Camrah means ember (kor, köz).

claims.quote: Celal Beydili'ne göre; bazı sözlüklerde gösterildiği gibi, Arap dilinden geldiğini söylemek doğru değildir.

statement.id: Menurut Celal Beydili, tidak benar mengatakan bahwa kata Cemre berasal dari bahasa Arab (Arap dilinden), seperti yang tertulis di beberapa kamus.
statement.en: According to Celal Beydili, it is not correct to say, as some dictionaries do, that the word Cemre comes from Arabic (Arap dilinden).

claims.quote: In Turkish folklore, three embers sent by a genie fall from the heavens at the end of the winter, and in turn, warm up the air, the water and the earth, one by one.

statement.id: Dalam folklor Turki (Turkish folklore), tiga bara yang dikirim oleh jin (genie) jatuh dari langit pada akhir musim dingin dan menghangatkan udara, air, dan tanah satu per satu.
statement.en: In Turkish folklore, three embers sent by a genie fall from the heavens at the end of winter and warm the air, the water and the earth one by one.

claims.quote: Arapça olan sözcük kor durumunda ateş anlamına gelir.

statement.id: Artikel ketiga menyebut kata Cemre berasal dari bahasa Arab (Arapça) dan berarti api dalam keadaan bara (kor).
statement.en: The third article says the word Cemre is Arabic (Arapça) and means fire in the state of embers (kor).

summary.id: Kata Cemre berasal dari bahasa Arab dan berarti bara; menurut artikel pertama, kata Arab itu berubah bentuk karena kemiripan dengan nama İmrə.
summary.en: The word Cemre comes from Arabic and means ember; according to the first article, that Arabic word changed by analogy with the name İmrə.

summary.id: Menurut Celal Beydili, tidak benar mengatakan kata itu berasal dari bahasa Arab.
summary.en: According to Celal Beydili, it is wrong to say the word comes from Arabic.

short_description.id: Imsety adalah dewa pelindung dalam agama Mesir kuno, salah satu dari Empat Putra Horus, berkepala manusia dan menjaga hati orang yang meninggal.
short_description.en: Imsety is a protector god of ancient Egyptian religion, one of the Four Sons of Horus, human-headed and guarding the liver of the deceased.

long_description.id: Imsety adalah salah satu dari Empat Putra Horus. Ia berkepala manusia, menjaga hati orang yang meninggal, dan dilindungi oleh dewi Isis. Paling umum ia melindungi hati, meskipun pola pembagian organ di antara keempat putra Horus sering berbeda-beda.
long_description.en: Imsety is one of the Four Sons of Horus. He has a human head, guards the liver of the deceased and is protected by the goddess Isis. Most commonly he protected the liver, although the division of organs among the four sons of Horus often varied.

long_description.id: Pada akhir Kerajaan Baru, Imsety digambarkan sebagai manusia, sedangkan Hapy berwujud babun, Duamutef jakal, dan Qebehsenuef elang. Dalam pasal 148 Kitab Orang Mati, keempat putra Horus dikaitkan dengan empat arah mata angin, dan Imsety sesuai dengan selatan.
long_description.en: In the latter part of the New Kingdom Imsety is portrayed as a human, while Hapy is a baboon, Duamutef a jackal and Qebehsenuef a falcon. In chapter 148 of the Book of the Dead the four sons of Horus are matched with the four directions, and Imsety corresponds to the south.

long_description.id: Imsety (jmstj, juga Amset) pertama kali disebut dalam Teks Piramida pada akhir Kerajaan Lama, dan dalam banyak sumber ia dinyatakan sebagai anak Horus. Egiptolog James P. Allen menerjemahkan namanya sebagai "Ia dari Dill", dan Joshua Roberson berpendapat ia bermula sebagai personifikasi herba itu. Namanya juga mirip kata Mesir untuk "hati", yang mungkin menjadi alasan keterkaitannya dengan organ tersebut.
long_description.en: Imsety (jmstj, also Amset) is first mentioned in the Pyramid Texts in the late Old Kingdom, and in numerous sources he is stated to be a child of Horus. The Egyptologist James P. Allen translates his name as "He of the Dill", and Joshua Roberson believes he originated as a personification of this herb. His name also resembled the Egyptian word for "liver", which may be why he became linked with that organ.

literal_meaning.en: "He of the Dill" (James P. Allen's translation)

claims.quote: The four sons of Horus were a group of four deities in ancient Egyptian religion ... Although they were originally portrayed as humans, in the latter part of the New Kingdom (c. 1550–1070 BC), they took on their most distinctive iconography, in which Imsety is portrayed as a human, Hapy as a baboon, Duamutef as a jackal, and Qebehsenuef as a falcon.

statement.id: Pada akhir Kerajaan Baru keempat putra Horus mengambil ikonografi khas mereka: Imsety digambarkan sebagai manusia, Hapy sebagai babun, Duamutef sebagai jakal, dan Qebehsenuef sebagai elang; sebelumnya mereka digambarkan sebagai manusia.
statement.en: In the latter part of the New Kingdom the four sons took on their most distinctive iconography: Imsety is portrayed as a human, Hapy as a baboon, Duamutef as a jackal and Qebehsenuef as a falcon; they had originally been portrayed as humans.

short_description.id: Ipilja-ipilja adalah tokek raksasa dalam mitologi Anindilyakwa di Groote Eylandt yang dianggap pencipta hujan dan guntur.
short_description.en: The ipilja-ipilja is a giant gecko in Anindilyakwa mythology on Groote Eylandt, considered the creator of rain and thunder.

long_description.id: Ipilja-ipilja, atau ipilya, adalah tokek raksasa dalam mitologi masyarakat Anindilyakwa di Australia, yang dianggap sebagai pencipta hujan dan guntur. Ia tinggal bersama keluarganya, semuanya tokek raksasa, di rawa Numarika di muara Angoroko River di Groote Eylandt.
long_description.en: The ipilja-ipilja (ipilya) is a giant gecko of Anindilyakwa mythology in Australia, regarded as the maker of rain and thunder. His home, shared with his family of giant geckos, is the Numarika swamp where the Angoroko River meets the sea on Groote Eylandt.

long_description.id: Para tokek itu berwarna-warni; ipilja-ipilja panjangnya sekitar seratus kaki dan berhias rambut serta kumis panjang. Pada awal musim monsun ia memakan rumput di tepi rawa dan meminum banyak air rawa, lalu menyemburkannya ke langit; air itu menjadi awan yang diikat rumput, dan ia, senang dengan hasilnya, mengeluarkan auman yang menjadi guntur.
long_description.en: The geckos are brightly coloured; the ipilja-ipilja is roughly a hundred feet long, with long hair and whiskers. At the start of the monsoon he eats grass from the swamp edge and drinks much swamp water, then spews it skyward; the water forms clouds held together by the grass, and, satisfied, he roars, and the roar is thunder.

long_description.id: Encyclopedia Mythica menyebut ipilja-ipilja sebagai tokek berwarna-warni di Groote Eylandt yang menggantikan Rainbow Serpent, yang menciptakan badai, guntur, dan hujan monsun.
long_description.en: Encyclopedia Mythica describes the ipilja-ipilja as the colorful gecko on Groote Eylandt who replaces the Rainbow Serpent and creates storms, thunder and the monsoon rains.

short_description.id: Jengu (jamak: miengu) adalah roh air mirip putri duyung dalam kepercayaan tradisional kelompok Sawabantu di Kamerun, yang dipuja karena membawa keberuntungan dan menyembuhkan penyakit.
short_description.en: In the old faith of the Sawabantu peoples of Cameroon, a jengu (plural miengu) is a mermaid-like spirit of the waters, honoured because it brings luck and cures illness.

long_description.id: Jengu, jamaknya miengu, adalah roh air dalam kepercayaan tradisional kelompok Sawabantu di Kamerun, antara lain Duala, Bakweri, Malimba, Subu, Bakoko, dan Oroko. Di kalangan Bakweri roh ini disebut liengu, jamaknya maengu. Miengu tinggal di sungai dan laut, dan dipandang sebagai penjaga alam.
long_description.en: Among the Sawabantu groups of Cameroon, including the Duala, Bakweri, Malimba, Subu, Bakoko and Oroko, a jengu (plural miengu) is a spirit that dwells in the water. The Bakweri call such a spirit liengu, plural maengu. Miengu live in rivers and the sea and are regarded as guardians of the natural world.

long_description.id: Wujud miengu berbeda menurut suku, tetapi biasanya mereka cantik, mirip putri duyung, berambut panjang, dan bergigi renggang yang indah. Mereka dibandingkan dengan Mami Wata, meski kepercayaan pada miengu diduga lebih tua. Dalam sebagian tradisi, Jengu adalah satu dewa yang menggantikan atau memimpin miengu; orang Isubu menggambarkannya sebagai lelaki berkaki terbalik.
long_description.en: Miengu look different from group to group, but they are usually lovely, mermaid-like beings with long hair and attractive gap-teeth. They are compared with Mami Wata, though belief in miengu is thought to be older. In some traditions Jengu is a single god who replaces or leads the miengu; the Isubu picture him as a man whose feet point backwards.

long_description.id: Miengu diyakini membawa keberuntungan, menyembuhkan penyakit, dan menjadi perantara antara manusia dan dunia roh. Pemujaan jengu sudah mapan pada awal abad ke-19, dan para misionaris awal gagal menekannya. Kini upacara terpentingnya adalah perayaan Ngondo tahunan di Douala, yang pertama kali digelar pada 1949: seorang anggota kultus menyelam ke laut membawa persembahan, lalu kembali dengan pesan tentang tahun mendatang.
long_description.en: Miengu are believed to bring luck, heal illness and carry messages between people and the spirit world. Jengu worship was firmly in place by the early 19th century, and early missionaries could not stamp it out. Today its best-known rite is the yearly Ngondo festival of Douala, held for the first time in 1949: a cult member dives into the sea with an offering and comes back with word about the year ahead.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan Bakweri mengenal dewi Mojili atau Mojele. Ia kalah taruhan dengan Moto, leluhur umat manusia, tentang siapa yang bisa membuat api paling lama menyala, sehingga terpaksa lari ke laut dan menjadi leluhur maengu. Orang Bakweri masih memujanya sebagai penguasa maengu.
long_description.en: Bakweri belief tells of a goddess, Mojili or Mojele. She lost a bet with Moto, ancestor of mankind, over who could keep a fire burning longer, and so had to flee to the sea, becoming the ancestor of the maengu. The Bakweri still worship her as their ruler.

cultural_context.id: Miengu dipuja karena dianggap membawa keberuntungan, menyembuhkan penyakit, dan menjadi perantara dengan dunia roh; perayaan Ngondo di Douala adalah upacara terpentingnya kini.
cultural_context.en: Miengu are worshipped as bringers of luck, healers and go-betweens with the spirit world; the Ngondo celebration in Douala is their chief ceremony today.

short_description.id: Jenu adalah raksasa berbulu yang liar dan kanibal dalam cerita rakyat Mi'kmaq [jenu-c01].
short_description.en: A Jenu is a wild, cannibalistic hairy giant of Mi'kmaq folklore [jenu-c01].

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Mi'kmaq, Jenu adalah raksasa berbulu yang liar dan kanibal [jenu-c01]. Sebuah ensiklopedia budaya menyebut Jenu sebagai "raksasa es dari utara" yang tetap hidup dalam kepercayaan Micmac berdampingan dengan kepercayaan Kristen [jenu-c06]. Namanya juga dieja Chenoo, Chenu, Jinu, Chinu, Djenu, dan Tsi-noo [jenu-c07].
long_description.en: In Mi'kmaq folklore, a Jenu is a wild, cannibalistic hairy giant [jenu-c01]. A cultural encyclopedia lists Jenu among the "northern ice giants" that live on in Micmac belief alongside Christian belief [jenu-c06]. The name is also spelled Chenoo, Chenu, Jinu, Chinu, Djenu and Tsi-noo [jenu-c07].

long_description.id: Seseorang menjadi Jenu ketika membiarkan es masuk ke hatinya [jenu-c02]. Sumber lain menyebut ia dahulu manusia yang dirasuki roh jahat atau melakukan kejahatan berat, terutama kanibalisme atau menolak memberi makan orang yang kelaparan, sehingga hatinya menjadi es [jenu-c08]. Setelah berubah, Jenu tampak berbulu dan kurus kering dengan tulang mencuat dari kulit [jenu-c03]. Ia paling aktif pada musim dingin karena manusia kurang bergerak dan lebih mudah diburu [jenu-c04]. Dalam beberapa legenda manusia berhasil diselamatkan dari hati beku seorang Chenoo, tetapi biasanya satu-satunya jalan keluar setelah berubah adalah kematian [jenu-c09].
long_description.en: A Jenu is created when a human allows ice into their heart [jenu-c02]. Another source says a Chenoo was once a person taken over by an evil spirit or guilty of a grave wrong, such as cannibalism or refusing food to someone starving, which turned the heart to ice [jenu-c08]. Once transformed, a Jenu appears hairy and emaciated, with bones poking through the skin [jenu-c03]. It is most active in winter because humans move less and are easier to hunt [jenu-c04]. In a few legends a human has been rescued from the frozen heart of a Chenoo, but usually the only escape after transformation is death [jenu-c09].

long_description.id: Jenu dapat dibandingkan dengan Wendigo dari mitologi Anishinaabe dan Cree dan, dalam kadar lebih kecil, Sasquatch [jenu-c05]. Di suku lain, tokoh terkait disebut Kee-wakw (Abenaki), Windigo (Anishinabe), dan Wihtiko (Cree) [jenu-c10].
long_description.en: The Jenu is likened to the Wendigo of Anishinaabe and Cree mythology and, more loosely, to Sasquatch [jenu-c05]. In other tribes, related figures are called Kee-wakw (Abenaki), Windigo (Anishinabe) and Wihtiko (Cree) [jenu-c10].

cultural_context.en: Micmac religious belief is syncretic: non-Christian supernatural beings such as the Jenu live on alongside Christian belief [jenu-c06].

short_description.id: Jin Chan adalah kodok emas dalam tradisi Tiongkok yang dipakai sebagai lambang kemakmuran feng shui.
short_description.en: Jin Chan is the golden toad in Chinese tradition, used as a feng shui prosperity charm.

long_description.id: Jin Chan adalah kodok emas dalam tradisi Tiongkok yang dipakai sebagai lambang kemakmuran feng shui. Kisah menyebut kemunculannya saat bulan purnama dekat tempat yang akan menerima kabar baik.
long_description.en: Jin Chan is the golden toad in Chinese tradition, used as a feng shui prosperity charm. The tale places its appearance at a full moon near places about to receive good news.

long_description.id: Penggambarannya mencakup mata merah, tiga kaki, dan koin di mulut. Dalam feng shui, Jin Chan dipercaya menarik dan melindungi kekayaan. Kodok uang ini dihubungkan dengan Liu Haichan sebagai pendamping hewan sang xian.
long_description.en: Its portrayal includes red eyes, three legs, and a coin in its mouth. In feng shui belief, Jin Chan attracts and protects wealth. The money toad is associated with Liu Haichan as the immortal's animal companion.

long_description.id: Dua museum menjelaskan kodok berkaki tiga dalam kaitannya dengan tokoh abadi Tao Liu Haichan atau Liu Hai. Museum Seni Cleveland menyebut Liu Haichan sebagai tokoh abadi Tao yang kadang dimasukkan dalam Delapan Dewa Abadi, dan biasanya digambarkan bersama untaian koin dan kodok berkaki tiga yang juga melambangkan kekayaan. Label di Museum Nelson-Atkins menyebut Liu Hai sebagai roh kekayaan yang bermain dengan hewan peliharaannya, kodok berkaki tiga.
long_description.en: Two museums explain the three-legged toad in relation to the Daoist immortal Liu Haichan or Liu Hai. The Cleveland Museum of Art describes him as a Daoist immortal sometimes included among the Eight Immortals and says he is shown with a string of coins and a three-legged toad that likewise stands for wealth. A label at the Nelson-Atkins Museum calls Liu Hai a spirit of wealth playing with his pet, a three-legged toad.

note.id: Kodok uang dikaitkan dengan Liu Haichan sebagai hewan pendamping sang tokoh abadi; museum menyebut Liu Haichan biasanya ditemani kodok berkaki tiga.
note.en: The money toad is associated with Liu Haichan as the immortal's animal companion; museums say Liu Haichan is usually accompanied by a three-legged toad.

short_description.id: Julunggul atau Yurlunggur adalah Ular Agung bangsa Yolngu di Arnhem Land, piton yang menelan saudari-saudari Wawalag dan dikaitkan dengan lubang air, monsun, dan kesuburan musiman.
short_description.en: Julunggul or Yurlunggur is the great snake of the Yolngu of Arnhem Land, a python who swallowed the Wawalag sisters and is linked to water holes, the monsoon, and seasonal fertility.

long_description.id: Yurlunggur, juga ditulis Yurlungur, Yulunggur, Jurlungur, Julunggur, atau Julunggul, adalah nama "ular pelangi" menurut Murngin (kelompok Yolngu) di Arnhem Land timur laut. Sumber lain menyebutnya Yulunggul, Piton Agung dari Arnhem Land utara-tengah yang menelan saudari-saudari Wawalag dan anak mereka. Ular Pelangi sendiri adalah dewa yang umum dalam tradisi Aborigin Australia dan sering dipandang sebagai dewa pencipta.
long_description.en: Yurlunggur, also written Yurlungur, Yulunggur, Jurlungur, Julunggur or Julunggul, is the name of the "rainbow serpent" among the Murngin, a Yolngu group of north-eastern Arnhem Land. A second source names him Yulunggul and describes him as the Great Python of north-central Arnhem Land, said to have swallowed the Wawalag sisters along with their child. The Rainbow Serpent in general is a common deity in Aboriginal Australian traditions, often seen as a creator god.

long_description.id: Yulunggul paling sering dikenali sebagai jantan, walau satu versi dari timur laut menyebutnya betina dengan makna simbolis jantan; catatan Warner menyebut berbagai ular, biawak, dan siput sebagai anaknya; Yurlunggur dari Arnhem Land mungkin berbadan ganda. Ia selalu berada di lubang air khususnya, Mirara-minar dan Muruwul, tidak datang dari tempat lain, dan berkaitan dengan air tawar maupun air asin. Semua Ular mitos di wilayah itu disebut penjaga situs yang baik yang tahu siapa para pengelana itu.
long_description.en: Yulunggul is most often identified as male, though one northeastern version makes him female with symbolic male meaning, and Warner's account lists snakes, goannas and snails as his sons; the Yurlunggur of Arnhem Land may have a double body. He had always dwelt at his own water hole, Mirara-minar and Muruwul, rather than arriving from elsewhere, and is linked with both fresh and salt water. The mythic Snakes of that region are described as good site guardians who knew who the travellers were.

long_description.id: Ia disebut roh monsun, angin barat dan barat laut yang membawa hujan penyubur musim basah, dan "persatuannya" dengan Wawalag menjadikannya lambang kesuburan musiman. Dalam beberapa versi Milingimbi ia terbang melintasi negeri dengan Wawalag di dalam tubuhnya sambil menamai tempat dan membagikan dialek. Dalam satu versi, didjeridu Yulunggul menghidupkan kembali para saudari, tetapi Yulunggul marah, "membunuh" mereka, dan menelannya lagi; didjeridu dalam Kunapipi disebut adalah Yulunggul sendiri dan bunyinya suaranya.
long_description.en: He is called the spirit of the monsoon, the west and northwest wind bringing the fertilizing rains of the wet season, and his "union" with the Wawalag made him a symbol of seasonal fertility. In some Milingimbi versions he flies across the land with the Wawalag inside him, naming places and allocating dialects. In one version a Yulunggul didjeridu revives the sisters, but Yulunggul is angry, "kills" them and swallows them again; the didjeridu of Kunapipi is said to be Yulunggul himself, its sound his voice.

long_description.id: Wikipedia mencatat Yurlunggur dianggap "bapa agung", tetapi Encyclopedia of Religion menyebut Warner memakai istilah itu dan mungkin salah dengar ungkapan "ular agung". Ada pula pandangan berbeda tentang apakah Yulunggul perwujudan Ular Pelangi; di tempat yang menolaknya, dikatakan bahwa "Yulunggul terpisah: ia adalah dirinya sendiri".
long_description.en: Wikipedia records Yurlunggur as considered "the great father", but the Encyclopedia of Religion says Warner used that term and may have misheard the expression "great snake". There are also divergent views on whether Yulunggul is a Rainbow Snake manifestation; where this is rejected it is said that "Yulunggul is separate: he is himself".

cultural_context.id: Yulunggul menjadi penanda budaya: setelah menelan Wawalag, ia menghadap timur dan berbicara dengan Ular-Ular besar lain yang berbagi komitmen religius yang sama.
cultural_context.en: Yulunggul is a cultural marker: after swallowing the Wawalag he faces east and talks with the other great Snakes who share the same religious commitments.

description.en: In some Milingimbi versions Yulunggul flies across the land with the Wawalag inside him; one version adds a didjeridu that revives the sisters.

summary.en: Yulunggul swallows the Wawalag sisters and their child; in one Milingimbi version he regurgitates them, his didjeridu revives them, but he is angry and swallows them again.

note.id: Yurlunggur disebut nama ular pelangi menurut Murngin, tetapi ada pandangan berbeda apakah Yulunggul perwujudan Ular Pelangi.
note.en: Yurlunggur is named as the rainbow serpent by the Murngin, but there are divergent views on whether Yulunggul is a Rainbow Snake manifestation.

claims.quote: The Rainbow Serpent or Rainbow Snake is a common deity, often seen as the creator god, known by numerous names in different Australian Aboriginal languages by the many different Aboriginal peoples.

statement.id: Ular Pelangi adalah dewa umum yang kerap dipandang sebagai dewa pencipta dalam masyarakat Aborigin Australia.
statement.en: The Rainbow Serpent is a common creator deity in Australian Aboriginal traditions.

claims.quote: Yurlunggur is the name of the "rainbow serpent" according to the Murngin (a Yolngu group) in north-eastern Arnhem Land, also styled Yurlungur, Yulunggur, Jurlungur, Julunggur or Julunggul.

statement.id: Julunggul atau Yurlunggur adalah nama ular pelangi bagi kelompok Murngin (Yolngu) di Arnhem Land.
statement.en: Julunggul or Yurlunggur is the name of the rainbow serpent among the Murngin (Yolngu) in Arnhem Land.

claims.quote: The Yurlunggur was considered "the great father".

statement.id: Yurlunggur dianggap sebagai sosok 'sang bapa agung'.
statement.en: The Yurlunggur was regarded as the great father.

claims.quote: While it is single-headed, the Yurlunggur of Arnhem land may possess a double-body.

statement.id: Meskipun berkepala tunggal, Yurlunggur dari Arnhem Land mungkin berbadan ganda.
statement.en: While single-headed, the Yurlunggur of Arnhem Land may possess a double body.

claims.quote: Yulunggul is the Great Python of north-central Arnhem Land, who swallowed the Wawalag sisters and their child(ren).

statement.id: Yulunggul adalah Piton Agung dari Arnhem Land bagian utara-tengah, yang menelan saudari-saudari Wawalag beserta anak mereka.
statement.en: Yulunggul is the Great Python of north-central Arnhem Land, who swallowed the Wawalag sisters and their child(ren).

claims.quote: Yulunggul is most often identified as male, with or without female counterparts. One northeastern Arnhem Land version specifies Yulunggul as female but with symbolic male (phallic) implications.

statement.id: Yulunggul paling sering dikenali sebagai jantan, dengan atau tanpa pasangan betina; satu versi dari timur laut Arnhem Land menyebutnya betina tetapi bermakna simbolis jantan (falus).
statement.en: Yulunggul is most often identified as male, with or without female counterparts; one northeastern Arnhem Land version has Yulunggul as female but with symbolic male (phallic) implications.

claims.quote: William Lloyd Warner's account (1937, e.g. p. 257) notes a variety of snakes, goannas, and snails as sons of Yulunggul.

statement.id: Catatan William Lloyd Warner (1937) menyebut berbagai ular, biawak, dan siput sebagai anak-anak Yulunggul.
statement.en: William Lloyd Warner's 1937 account notes a variety of snakes, goannas, and snails as sons of Yulunggul.

claims.quote: Warner refers to Yulunggul as "great father" (Yindi Bapa or Bapa Yindi), but it is possible that he misheard the more usual expression, "great snake" (Yindi Baapi).

statement.id: Warner menyebut Yulunggul "bapa agung" (Yindi Bapa atau Bapa Yindi), tetapi mungkin ia salah dengar ungkapan yang lebih lazim, "ular agung" (Yindi Baapi).
statement.en: Warner calls Yulunggul "great father" (Yindi Bapa or Bapa Yindi), but he may have misheard the more usual expression "great snake" (Yindi Baapi).

claims.quote: Unlike so many of the great mythic characters, who came from elsewhere to sites that were to be spiritually associated with them, Yulunggul had always been at his special water hole, known as Mirara-minar and Muruwul;

statement.id: Berbeda dari banyak tokoh mitos besar yang datang dari tempat lain, Yulunggul selalu berada di lubang air khususnya, yang dikenal sebagai Mirara-minar dan Muruwul.
statement.en: Unlike many great mythic characters who came from elsewhere, Yulunggul had always been at his special water hole, known as Mirara-minar and Muruwul.

claims.quote: all of the mythic Snakes in north and northeastern Arnhem Land, including Yulunggul, were good site guardians and knew who the travelers were.

statement.id: Semua Ular mitos di Arnhem Land utara dan timur laut, termasuk Yulunggul, adalah penjaga situs yang baik dan tahu siapa para pengelana itu.
statement.en: All the mythic Snakes in north and northeastern Arnhem Land, including Yulunggul, were good site guardians and knew who the travellers were.

claims.quote: There are divergent views on whether Yulunggul is a Rainbow Snake manifestation.

statement.id: Ada pandangan yang berbeda tentang apakah Yulunggul merupakan perwujudan Ular Pelangi.
statement.en: There are divergent views on whether Yulunggul is a Rainbow Snake manifestation.

claims.quote: Where his Rainbow Snake identification is not accepted, mainly on the eastern side of Arnhem Land, it is sometimes explained with, "Yulunggul is separate: he is himself."

statement.id: Di tempat identifikasinya sebagai Ular Pelangi tidak diterima, terutama di sisi timur Arnhem Land, kadang dijelaskan bahwa "Yulunggul terpisah: ia adalah dirinya sendiri".
statement.en: Where his Rainbow Snake identification is not accepted, mainly in eastern Arnhem Land, it is sometimes explained: "Yulunggul is separate: he is himself."

claims.quote: He is the spirit of the monsoon, the west and northwest wind that brings the fertilizing rains of the wet season.

statement.id: Ia adalah roh musim hujan monsun, angin barat dan barat laut yang membawa hujan penyubur musim basah.
statement.en: He is the spirit of the monsoon, the west and northwest wind that brings the fertilizing rains of the wet season.

claims.quote: In some Milingimbi versions (Warner, p. 254), he flies across the country with the Wawalag and their child(ren) inside him, naming various places and allocating local dialects.

statement.id: Dalam beberapa versi Milingimbi, ia terbang melintasi negeri dengan Wawalag dan anak mereka di dalam tubuhnya, menamai berbagai tempat dan membagikan dialek setempat.
statement.en: In some Milingimbi versions he flies across the country with the Wawalag and their child(ren) inside him, naming various places and allocating local dialects.

claims.quote: Just as the copulations of the Snakes and clouds during the wet season ensure fertility in the dry season, so Yulunggul's "union" with the Wawalag transformed him into a symbol of seasonal fertility.

statement.id: Seperti persetubuhan para Ular dan awan pada musim basah menjamin kesuburan musim kering, "persatuan" Yulunggul dengan Wawalag menjadikannya lambang kesuburan musiman.
statement.en: Just as the copulations of the Snakes and clouds in the wet season ensure fertility in the dry season, Yulunggul's "union" with the Wawalag made him a symbol of seasonal fertility.

claims.quote: The didjeridu that features so prominently in Kunapipi and associated rituals, however, is Yulunggul, and its sound is his voice.

statement.id: Didjeridu yang menonjol dalam Kunapipi dan ritual terkait adalah Yulunggul, dan bunyinya adalah suaranya.
statement.en: The didjeridu that features so prominently in Kunapipi and associated rituals is Yulunggul, and its sound is his voice.

claims.quote: in a Milingimbi version that is found only in Warner, after Yulunggul had regurgitated the sisters and they lay "dead," a great Yulunggul didjeridu (drone pipe) came out of Yulunggul's water hole of its own volition and revived them with the help of green ants. Yulunggul was angry. He "killed" the sisters and swallowed them again.

statement.id: Dalam satu versi Milingimbi, didjeridu Yulunggul keluar dari lubang airnya dan menghidupkan kembali para saudari dengan bantuan semut hijau; Yulunggul marah, "membunuh" mereka, dan menelannya lagi.
statement.en: In a Milingimbi version, a great Yulunggul didjeridu came out of his water hole and revived the sisters with the help of green ants; Yulunggul was angry, "killed" them and swallowed them again.

claims.quote: He has both freshwater and saltwater affiliations.

statement.id: Yulunggul berkaitan dengan air tawar maupun air asin.
statement.en: Yulunggul has both freshwater and saltwater affiliations.

claims.quote: In one of his roles Yulunggul is, explicitly, a culture-area indicator, or a boundary marker. During his conversation with the other great Snakes after he has swallowed the Wawalag, he faces east.

statement.id: Dalam salah satu perannya Yulunggul secara eksplisit adalah penanda wilayah budaya atau batas; dalam percakapannya dengan Ular besar lain setelah menelan Wawalag, ia menghadap timur.
statement.en: In one of his roles Yulunggul is explicitly a culture-area indicator or boundary marker; in his conversation with the other great Snakes after swallowing the Wawalag he faces east.

short_description.id: Ka'a Póra (Caapóra) adalah makhluk dalam mitologi suku-suku Tupi yang dikenal sebagai wanita hantu atau pria raksasa, pemilik dan pelindung hewan hutan yang membantu atau menggagalkan para pemburu.
short_description.en: Ka'a Póra (Caapóra) is a creature of Tupi mythology known as a ghost woman or an enormous man, owner and protector of the forest animals who can help or thwart hunters.

long_description.id: Ka'a Póra, juga ditulis Caapóra atau Caá Póra, adalah makhluk dari mitologi suku-suku Tupi. Namanya berasal dari bahasa Guaraní: ka'a berarti antara lain daun, tumbuhan, atau hutan, dan póra diterjemahkan sebagai hantu, sehingga nama ini berarti hantu hutan atau roh hutan.
long_description.en: Ka'a Póra, also written Caapóra or Caá Póra, is a creature of the mythology of the Tupi tribes. Its name comes from Guaraní: ka'a means among other things leaf, plant or forest, and póra is translated as ghost, so the name means ghost of the forest or forest spirit.

long_description.id: Sosok ini berwujud wanita hantu di negara bagian Rio Grande do Sul dan di selatan Paraguay, atau pria raksasa di timur laut Argentina. Di antara kelompok non-Guaraní ia disebut Kripandufuá.
long_description.en: It takes the form of a ghost woman in the state of Rio Grande do Sul and in southern Paraguay, or of an enormous man in northeastern Argentina. Among non-Guaraní groups it is called Kripandufuá.

long_description.id: Dalam penggambarannya sebagai wanita, Ka'a Póra adalah pemilik dan pelindung hewan hutan. Jika ia berhubungan baik dengan seorang pemburu, ia dapat membantunya; jika tidak, ia akan memukuli anjing-anjing pemburu itu dengan memanfaatkan ketakkasatmataannya sehingga buruan lolos.
long_description.en: In its portrayal as a woman, the Ka'a Póra is owner and protector of the forest animals. If she is on good terms with a hunter she can help him; if not, she uses her invisibility to beat his dogs so that the prey escapes.

long_description.id: Ambrosetti dalam bukunya mencatat beberapa versi Caá-Porá. Di Río Grande del Sur ia wanita pemilik hewan hutan, sejenis Diana; di Paraná ia pria berbulu lebat, raksasa, berkepala besar. Bagi sebagian orang ia pria berbulu yang mengisap pipa dari tengkorak manusia dan tulang kering serta melahap orang, dan dalam penuturan lain ia sekadar Porá, hantu berwujud babi atau anjing yang menyemburkan api dari mulut. Ia sendiri berpendapat bahwa imajinasi para penghuni hutan yang terlalu bersemangat memberi bentuk manusia pada batang-batang pohon.
long_description.en: In his book Ambrosetti recorded several versions of the Caá-Porá. In Río Grande del Sur it is a woman who owns the forest animals, a kind of Diana; in Paraná it is a hairy, gigantic man with a large head. For some it is a hairy man who smokes a pipe made from a human skull and a tibia and devours people, and in other accounts it is simply Porá, a ghost in the shape of a pig or dog that spits flames from its mouth. He himself suggests that the overexcited imagination of woodsmen gives human forms to tree trunks.

short_description.id: Kaimingshou adalah makhluk ilahi dalam bagian Hai Nei Xi Jing pada Shan Hai Jing.
short_description.en: Kaimingshou is a divine creature in the Hai Nei Xi Jing section of the Shan Hai Jing.

long_description.id: Kaimingshou adalah makhluk ilahi dalam bagian Hai Nei Xi Jing pada Shan Hai Jing. Ia menjaga sembilan gerbang Kunlun, kediaman penguasa langit di dunia bawah.
long_description.en: Kaimingshou is a divine creature in the Hai Nei Xi Jing section of the Shan Hai Jing. It guards the nine gates of Kunlun, the heavenly ruler's dwelling in the lower world.

long_description.id: Tubuhnya besar dan menyerupai harimau. Kesembilan kepalanya mempunyai wajah manusia. Uraian tentang satu gerbang utama timur disebut tidak terdapat dalam Shan Hai Jing. Kaimingshou kadang disamakan dengan Lu Wu karena kemiripan sifatnya.
long_description.en: Its body is large and tigerlike. Its nine heads each have a human face. The description of a single principal eastern gate is identified as absent from the Shan Hai Jing. Kaimingshou is sometimes identified with Lu Wu because of their similar characteristics.

long_description.id: Teks primer Shanhaijing, bagian Haineixi Jing, menyebut 昆侖之虛 memiliki sembilan gerbang dan tiap gerbang dijaga 開明獸. Teks itu menggambarkan 開明獸 bertubuh besar mirip harimau dengan sembilan kepala berwajah manusia, berdiri di atas Kunlun menghadap ke timur.
long_description.en: The primary text of the Shanhaijing, in the Overseas-West-within section, says the 昆侖之虛 has nine gates, each guarded by the 開明獸. It describes the 開明獸 as large and tiger-like with nine human-faced heads, standing on Kunlun facing east.

short_description.id: El Familiar adalah roh berwujud anjing hitam raksasa dari pabrik gula Argentina barat laut yang memberi kekayaan kepada pemilik pabrik dengan imbalan nyawa pekerja.
short_description.en: El Familiar is a huge black dog spirit of the sugar mills of north-western Argentina that brings mill owners wealth in exchange for workers' lives.

long_description.id: El Familiar adalah roh pendamping pemakan manusia yang legendanya tersebar di pabrik gula Argentina barat laut. Ia paling sering digambarkan sebagai anjing hitam raksasa setinggi manusia dengan mata menyala, dan pada malam hari dapat menjadi ular yang melingkari barak pekerja. Ia memberi kekuasaan dan uang kepada pemiliknya dengan imbalan nyawa manusia.
long_description.en: El Familiar is a man-eating familiar spirit whose legend is widespread in the sugar mills of north-western Argentina. It is most often a huge black dog as tall as a man with blazing eyes, and at night it can become a snake coiling round the workers' sheds. It gives its owner power and money in exchange for human lives.

long_description.id: Legenda ini sering melibatkan perjanjian pemilik pabrik dengan Iblis, dibayar dengan nyawa pekerja; Ingenio Santa Ana di Tucumán disebut yang pertama memilikinya. Hilangnya para pekerja di masa kediktatoran pun dikaitkan dengan El Familiar.
long_description.en: The legend often involves a pact between mill owners and the Devil, paid for with workers' lives; the Ingenio Santa Ana in Tucumán is said to have been the first to have one. Workers' disappearances under the dictatorship were also blamed on El Familiar.

statement.en: El Familiar, also known as El cuñado, El Tío or Perro Familiar, is a man-eating familiar spirit whose legend is widespread in the sugar mills of north-western Argentina.

claims.quote: Se han descrito diferentes versiones de esta entidad, pero la más conocida lo identifica con una especie de criatura demoníaca con aspecto de cánido que da poder y dinero a su poseedor a cambio, generalmente, de vidas humanas.

statement.id: Versi paling terkenal menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk iblis berwujud anjing yang memberi kekuasaan dan uang kepada pemiliknya dengan imbalan, biasanya, nyawa manusia.
statement.en: The best-known version makes it a demonic dog-like creature that gives its owner power and money in exchange, usually, for human lives.

claims.quote: A veces, la leyenda involucra un pacto entre los dueños de los ingenios y el Diablo, que asegura la prevalencia de su estatus socioeconómico a cambio de sus almas y de la vida de algunos de sus trabajadores, arrebatadas periódicamente por el Familiar.

statement.id: Kadang legenda ini melibatkan perjanjian antara pemilik pabrik gula dan Iblis yang menjamin kedudukan mereka dengan imbalan jiwa mereka dan nyawa sebagian pekerja, yang diambil El Familiar secara berkala.
statement.en: Sometimes the legend involves a pact between the mill owners and the Devil, securing their status in exchange for their souls and the lives of some workers, taken periodically by the Familiar.

claims.quote: Muchas desapariciones de zafreros del Ingenio Ledesma y otros sucedidas durante el Proceso de Reorganización Nacional han sido vinculadas con el accionar del Familiar.

statement.id: Banyak hilangnya pekerja tebu di Ingenio Ledesma dan pabrik lain pada masa kediktatoran Proceso de Reorganización Nacional dikaitkan dengan El Familiar.
statement.en: Many disappearances of cane workers at the Ingenio Ledesma and other mills during the Proceso de Reorganización Nacional dictatorship have been linked to the Familiar.

short_description.id: Kaldaz (Kaldaz Xanım) adalah dewi api dalam mitologi Turk dan Altai; menurut pandangan lain ia pelindung ternak dan hewan bertanduk besar.
short_description.en: Kaldaz (Kaldaz Xanım) is a goddess of fire in Turkic and Altaic mythology; according to another view she is the protector of livestock and large horned animals.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel pertama, Kaldaz xanım adalah dewi api dalam mitologi Turk dan Altai. Kamus kedua menyebutnya pelindung api. Kedua sumber mencatat pandangan lain bahwa ia melindungi ternak dan hewan besar.
long_description.en: According to the first article, Kaldaz xanım is a goddess of fire in Turkic and Altaic mythology. The second source, a dictionary, calls her the protector of fire. Both sources record another view in which she protects livestock and large animals.

long_description.id: Makhluk yang berada di bawah perintahnya diberi nama Kaldazın. Sebagai entri tersendiri, Kaldazın digambarkan sebagai jin api yang bermain di dalam api, bertubuh pendek, berjanggut tujuh jengkal yang seperti duri landak, dan dapat berubah menjadi sable kuning.
long_description.en: The beings under her command are given the name Kaldazın. As an entry of their own, the Kaldazın is described as a fire jinn that plays in the fire, is short, has a seven-span beard like hedgehog quills, and can turn into a yellow sable.

long_description.id: Namanya dijelaskan sebagai gabungan kata Kal, yang berarti api atau botak, dan Daz, yang berarti botak atau tak berambut.
long_description.en: Her name is explained as a combination of the words Kal, meaning fire or bald, and Daz, meaning bald or hairless.

literal_meaning.id: Kal berarti api (atəş) dan Daz berarti botak (keçəl); sumber kedua memberi Kal sebagai Kel atau Ateş dan Daz sebagai Saçsız.
literal_meaning.en: Kal means fire (atəş) and Daz means bald (keçəl); the second source gives Kal as Kel or Ateş and Daz as Saçsız.

long_description.id: Kisah Krishna dan Kaliya terdapat dalam Bhagavata Purana canto sepuluh bab enam belas. Ia meninggalkan tempat asalnya di Ramanaka karena takut pada Garuda. Krishna menari di atas kepala Kaliya untuk mengeluarkan racunnya sehingga tidak lagi mencemari Yamuna. Dalam Bhagavata versi Vedabase, Krishna memerintahkan Kaliya meninggalkan sungai bersama keluarga dan kembali ke Ramanaka.
long_description.en: The Krishna and Kaliya account appears in Bhagavata Purana canto ten chapter sixteen. He leaves his Ramanaka homeland in fear of Garuda. Krishna dances on Kaliya's heads to release his poison so he no longer pollutes the Yamuna. In the Vedabase Bhagavata version Krishna orders Kaliya to leave the river with his family and return to Ramanaka.

short_description.id: Kallikantzaros adalah makhluk jahat dalam cerita rakyat Yunani modern yang hidup di bawah tanah dan naik ke permukaan selama dua belas hari Natal.
short_description.en: The kallikantzaros is a malevolent creature of modern Greek folklore that lives underground and comes to the surface during the twelve days of Christmas.

long_description.id: Kallikantzaros adalah makhluk jahat dalam cerita rakyat Yunani modern. Menurut kepercayaan, mereka tinggal di bawah tanah dan menghabiskan sebagian besar waktu mencoba menggergaji pohon raksasa penyangga bumi, tetapi naik ke permukaan selama dua belas hari Natal, dari 25 Desember sampai 6 Januari. Padanannya juga ditemukan dalam tradisi Bulgaria.
long_description.en: The kallikantzaros is a malevolent creature in modern Greek folklore. Belief holds that they dwell underground, where they spend most of their time trying to cut down the huge tree that holds up the earth, yet they emerge during the twelve days of Christmas, 25 December to 6 January. Counterparts are also found in Bulgarian tradition.

long_description.id: Sebuah kajian lama tentang cerita rakyat Yunani menambahkan bahwa selama sisa tahun mereka berada di dunia bawah, berusaha menggerogoti atau menebang pohon besar (atau satu atau beberapa tiang) tempat dunia bertumpu. Tiap Natal tugas itu hampir rampung ketika tiba saat mereka naik ke dunia atas, dan selama dua belas hari mereka pergi, penopang dunia pulih kembali.
long_description.en: An old study of Greek folklore adds that for the rest of the year they stay in the lower world, working to gnaw through or cut down the great tree (or one or more columns) on which the world rests. Each Christmas the task is nearly done when the time comes for them to go to the upper world, and during their twelve days away the supports of the world are made whole again.

long_description.id: Kajian itu melukiskan wajah mereka hitam, mata merah menyala, bertelinga kambing atau keledai, dengan lidah merah darah menjulur dari mulut besar berapit taring garang. Mereka sering pincang tetapi cepat berlari dan sangat kuat. Kajian itu juga membedakan jenis yang lebih besar, yang kadang jahat bahkan mematikan, dari jenis yang lebih kecil, yang lebih jenaka dan tidak berbahaya.
long_description.en: The study describes them with black faces, glaring red eyes, the ears of goats or asses, and blood-red tongues lolling from huge mouths flanked by ferocious tusks. They are often lame but swift of foot and terrible in strength. It also distinguishes a larger sort, whose mischief is sometimes malicious and even deadly, from a smaller sort, which is more frolicsome and harmless.

long_description.id: Dari fajar hingga senja mereka bersembunyi di tempat gelap dan lembap, di gua atau di bawah kincir, dan makan cacing, ular, katak, kura-kura, serta hal-hal tak bersih lain. Mereka menyerbu rumah lewat cerobong dan pintu, menjungkirbalikkan dan mematahkan perabot, menyantap daging babi Natal, dan mengotori air, anggur, serta makanan yang tersisa. Menurut kajian itu, mereka lenyap saat ayam jantan ketiga berkokok, yang hitam dan lebih ampuh menakuti setan daripada ayam putih dan merah sebelumnya. Penulisnya menjelaskan keanehan uraian daerah-daerah itu dengan menyatakan bahwa mereka identik dengan Centaur kuno.
long_description.en: From dawn until sunset they hide in dark and dank places, in caves or beneath mills, and eat worms, snakes, frogs, tortoises and other unclean things. They swarm into homes by chimney and door, overturn and break the furniture, devour the Christmas pork, and befoul the water, wine and food that remain. According to the study they vanish when the third cock crows, the black one, which scares demons away better than the white and red cocks that crow before it. Its author explains the oddity of the regional accounts by stating that they are identical with the ancient Centaurs.
