short_description.id: Kamappa atau Kammapa, juga disebut Khanyapa dan Khodumodumo, adalah monster raksasa tanpa bentuk dalam cerita rakyat Basotho yang menelan hampir semua makhluk hidup sampai dikalahkan oleh pahlawan Ditaolane atau Litaolane.
short_description.en: Kamappa or Kammapa, also called Khanyapa and Khodumodumo, is a vast shapeless monster of Basotho folklore that swallows nearly every living thing until it is slain by the hero Ditaolane, or Litaolane.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Basotho, Kamappa adalah monster rakus yang tidak memiliki bentuk tetap. Ia menelan setiap makhluk hidup yang ditemuinya, dan tubuhnya terus membesar setiap kali ia makan. Ia juga disebut memiliki banyak lidah tajam yang dipakai sebagai senjata, dan tubuhnya begitu panjang sehingga mata paling tajam pun sukar melihatnya utuh sekaligus.
long_description.en: In Basotho folklore, Kamappa is a greedy monster without fixed form. It swallows every living creature it meets, and its body keeps growing with each meal. It is also said to have many sharp tongues that serve as weapons, and to be so long that even the keenest eyes can barely take it in at once.

long_description.id: Menurut kisahnya, monster itu melahap semua orang hingga hanya tersisa seorang perempuan yang bersembunyi dengan tubuh berlumur abu. Kamappa yang membengkak akhirnya tersangkut di celah gunung sempit. Perempuan itu melahirkan seorang anak yang seketika tumbuh dewasa dan bijak; anak itu pergi menghadapi sang monster, membiarkan dirinya ditelan, lalu merobek isi perut Kamappa dengan pisau hingga monster itu mati dan semua orang yang ditelannya keluar kembali.
long_description.en: In the tale, the monster devours everyone until only one woman remains, hidden with her body smeared in ashes. The swollen Kamappa finally becomes stuck in a narrow mountain pass. The woman bears a son who instantly grows into a wise adult; he goes to face the monster, lets himself be swallowed, then tears its entrails with a knife so that it dies and everyone it swallowed comes out again.

long_description.id: Nama Kgodumodumo kemungkinan berarti "suara besar" dalam bahasa Sotho kuno, dan para arkeolog menduga sosok ini dipengaruhi dewa piton orang San. Dalam penafsiran modern, monster ini melambangkan segala yang menghambat kemanusiaan. Misionaris Casalis, yang mencatat kisah ini, menyebut bahwa penduduk setempat sendiri tidak dapat menjelaskan legenda tersebut.
long_description.en: The name Kgodumodumo probably means "great noise" in archaic Sotho, and archeologists suspect the figure was influenced by the San people's python god. In modern interpretation the monster stands for all that holds humanity back. The missionary Casalis, who recorded the tale, noted that local people themselves could not explain the legend.

claims.quote: Once upon a time there appeared in our country a huge, shapeless thing called Khodumodumo (but some people call it Kammapa). It swallowed every living creature that came in its way.

short_description.id: Kāmohoaliʻi adalah dewa hiu dan uap dalam agama Hawaii, saudara Pele, yang dalam kisah lama disebut raja para hiu dan pemandu kapal yang tersesat.
short_description.en: Kāmohoaliʻi is a shark and steam god of Hawaiian religion, brother of Pele, called in older accounts the king of the sharks and a guide for lost ships.

long_description.id: Dalam agama Hawaii, Kāmohoaliʻi adalah dewa hiu dan uap serta saudara Pele dan Nāmaka. Westervelt menyebutnya raja para hiu, dan menulis bahwa ia kakak tertua serta penjaga keluarga Pele. Emerson mencatat bahwa dalam satu perubahan wujud ia berbentuk hiu.
long_description.en: In Hawaiian religion Kāmohoaliʻi is a shark and steam god and a brother of Pele and Nāmaka. Westervelt calls him king of the sharks and writes that he was the eldest brother and caretaker of Pele's family. Emerson notes that in one metamorphosis he took the form of a shark.

long_description.id: Ia berenang di perairan sekitar Maui dan Kahoʻolawe. Bila kapal hilang di laut, ia mengibaskan ekornya di depan armada dan menuntun para pelaut pulang setelah kahuna memberinya awa, minuman yang memabukkan.
long_description.en: He swam in the waters around Maui and Kahoʻolawe. When a ship was lost at sea he shook his tail before the fleet and led the men home after the kahuna gave him awa, a narcotic drink.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Westervelt, ia menyediakan perahu besar Honua-i-a-kea untuk membawa keluarga Pele ke pulau-pulau yang jauh, dan kadang-kadang berwujud hiu menjadi papan selancar Pele. Menurut Emerson, sebuah titik tinggi di dinding Kilauea dianggap tempat tinggalnya yang keramat.
long_description.en: In a tale recorded by Westervelt he provided the great boat Honua-i-a-kea to carry Pele's family to distant islands, and sometimes as a shark he served as Pele's surf-board. According to Emerson, a high point on the wall of Kilauea was held to be his sacred residence.

short_description.id: Kanedama adalah roh uang Jepang yang konon memakmurkan rumah.
short_description.en: Kanedama is a Japanese money spirit said to enrich a household.

long_description.id: Kanedama adalah roh uang Jepang yang konon memakmurkan rumah. Sekien menggambarkan koin memenuhi gudang rumah yang berbuat baik.
long_description.en: Kanedama is a Japanese money spirit said to enrich a household. Sekien depicts coins filling the storehouse of a virtuous household.

long_description.id: Satu tafsir menganggap gambar itu lambang ganjaran bagi kebajikan. Versi Kyōden mengunjungi orang jujur dan meninggalkan mereka yang dikuasai keserakahan.
long_description.en: One interpretation treats the image as a symbol of rewards for virtue. Kyōden’s version visits honest people and leaves those overcome by greed.

long_description.id: Sebuah catatan folklor dari Tokyo (1938) menyebut kanedama terbang sambil mengerang, dan rumah tempat ia jatuh makmur sedangkan rumah tempat ia keluar hancur. Catatan dari Numazu (1951) menyebut orang yang menyimpan kanedama di tokonoma menjadi kaya dalam satu generasi asalkan benda itu tidak diolah. Kamus Daijisen Plus mencatatnya sebagai sejenis api gaib yang membuat pemiliknya kaya.
long_description.en: A folklore record from Tokyo (1938) says the kanedama flies while groaning, and a house where it falls prospers while one from which it emerges is ruined. A record from Numazu (1951) says whoever keeps a kanedama in the tokonoma becomes rich within one generation as long as it is not worked. The Daijisen Plus dictionary records it as a kind of strange fire that makes its owner rich.

long_description.id: Dalam pustaka yōkai modern, Mizuki Shigeru mengaku pernah melihatnya sebagai koin 10 yen cokelat raksasa. Tada Katsumi menduga benda yang konon jatuh dari langit dalam salah satu kisah adalah meteorit besi. Zenigami, roh uang dalam Kokon Hyakumonogatari Hyōban, disebut makhluk sejenis.
long_description.en: In modern yōkai literature, Mizuki Shigeru said he once saw it as a giant brown 10-yen coin. Tada Katsumi guesses the object said to have fallen from the sky in one story was an iron meteorite. The zenigami, a coin spirit in the Kokon Hyakumonogatari Hyōban, is described as a similar kind of being.

note.id: Zenigami (銭神) disebut sebagai makhluk sejenis kanedama.
note.en: The zenigami (銭神) is described as a similar kind of being.

claims.quote: 1803年（享和3年）の山東京伝による草双紙『怪談摸摸夢字彙（かいだんももんじい）』では「金玉（かねだま）」の名で記載されており、正直者のもとに飛び込み、欲に溺れると去るものとされている。

statement.id: Versi Kyōden mengunjungi orang jujur dan meninggalkan mereka yang dikuasai keserakahan.
statement.en: Kyōden’s version visits honest people and leaves those overcome by greed.

claims.quote: カネダマは唸りながら飛ぶ。カネダマが出た家は滅び、カネダマが落ちた家は栄えると言う。

statement.id: Dalam catatan dari Distrik Adachi, Tokyo (1938), kanedama terbang sambil mengerang; rumah tempat kanedama keluar hancur, sedangkan rumah tempat ia jatuh makmur.
statement.en: In a record from Adachi Ward, Tokyo (1938), the kanedama flies while groaning; a house from which a kanedama emerges is said to fall into ruin, while a house where it falls prospers.

claims.quote: 金玉（かねだま）を拾って床の間に安置すると一代で大金持ちになれる。ただし自然のまま保存せねばならず、加工すると家が絶える。夜、赤い光を出しながら足元を転げていくという。

statement.id: Dalam catatan dari Numazu, Shizuoka (1951), orang yang menemukan kanedama dan menyimpannya di tokonoma akan menjadi kaya raya dalam satu generasi, tetapi benda itu harus dibiarkan alami karena bila diolah rumahnya punah; pada malam hari ia menggelinding di kaki sambil memancarkan cahaya merah.
statement.en: In a record from Numazu, Shizuoka (1951), whoever picks up a kanedama and keeps it in the tokonoma becomes very rich within one generation, but it must be kept in its natural state, since working it brings the house to an end; at night it is said to roll at one's feet giving off red light.

claims.quote: また水木は、自身も幼い頃に実際に金霊を目にしたと語っており、それによれば金霊の姿は、轟音とともに空を飛ぶ巨大な茶色い十円硬貨のような姿だったという。

statement.id: Mizuki Shigeru mengaku pernah melihat kanedama saat kecil, dan menggambarkannya seperti koin 10 yen cokelat raksasa yang terbang di langit dengan gemuruh keras.
statement.en: Mizuki Shigeru said he saw a kanedama himself as a child, describing it as like a giant brown 10-yen coin flying through the sky with a thunderous roar.

claims.quote: 同じく妖怪研究家の多田克己は、この空から落ちてきたという物体を、赤々と光っていたとのことから、隕鉄（金属質の隕石）と推測している。

statement.id: Peneliti yōkai Tada Katsumi menduga benda yang konon jatuh dari langit itu adalah meteorit besi karena disebut bersinar merah.
statement.en: The yōkai researcher Tada Katsumi guesses that the object said to have fallen from the sky was an iron meteorite, since it was described as glowing red.

claims.quote: 似た仲間に、江戸時代の怪談本『古今百物語評判』に記述されている「銭神（ぜにがみ）」がある。銭霊（ぜにだま）ともいい、黄昏時に世界中の銭の精が薄雲状となって人家の軒を通るもので、刀で切り落とすと大量の銭がこぼれ落ちるという。

statement.id: Makhluk sejenis adalah "zenigami" (銭神, juga zenidama) dalam buku cerita seram Edo Kokon Hyakumonogatari Hyōban: roh uang dunia yang membentuk kabut tipis lewat di bawah atap rumah saat senja, dan bila ditebas dengan pedang uang berhamburan.
statement.en: A similar kind is the "zenigami" (銭神, also zenidama) in the Edo-period ghost-story book Kokon Hyakumonogatari Hyōban: the spirits of the world's coins form a thin cloud passing the eaves of houses at dusk, and cutting it with a sword spills a great quantity of coins.

claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。怪火の一種で、手に入れたものは裕福になるとされる。「金玉」とも。

statement.id: Kamus Daijisen Plus mencatatnya sebagai yōkai Jepang, sejenis api gaib, yang membuat orang yang mendapatkannya menjadi kaya; juga disebut "kanedama" (金玉).
statement.en: The Daijisen Plus dictionary records it as a Japanese yōkai, a kind of strange fire, which makes whoever obtains it wealthy; it is also written "kanedama" (金玉).

short_description.id: Kangla sha adalah makhluk penjaga suci dalam mitologi Meitei, bertubuh singa dan berkepala naga bertanduk dua.
short_description.en: Kangla sha is a sacred guardian creature in Meitei mythology, with a lion's body and two-horned dragon head.

long_description.id: Kangla sha adalah makhluk penjaga suci dalam mitologi Meitei dan Sanamahism, agama asli Manipur, bertubuh singa dan berkepala naga bertanduk dua. Namanya berarti 'hewan Kangla'. Makhluk itu merupakan lambang kerajaan Meitei, dan menurut seorang penulis tentang Manipur ia adalah ikon mitos raja-raja Manipur.
long_description.en: Kangla sha is a guardian beast held sacred in Meitei mythology and in Sanamahism, the indigenous religion of Manipur; its body is a lion's and its head a dragon's with two horns. Its name means 'beast of the Kangla'. It serves as a Meitei royal symbol, and an author writing on Manipur calls it a myth-associated icon of the kings of Manipur.

long_description.id: Patung-patungnya di pintu masuk istana kerajaan menjadi tempat kehormatan bagi semua upacara kerajaan. Dalam lomba tradisional, pemenang baru dinyatakan setelah menyentuh patungnya secara simbolis, dan dalam lomba Lamchel menyentuh Kangla-Sha menjadi garis akhir.
long_description.en: Its statues at the entrance of the royal palace were the place of pride for all royal ceremonies. In traditional races, winners are declared only after symbolically touching its statue, and in the Lamchel race touching the Kangla-Sha is the finishing point.

long_description.id: Menurut Wikipedia, Chourjit Singh membangun dua patung pada 1804, dan pasukan Burma menghancurkannya pada masa Chahi Taret Khuntakpa (1819-1826). Raja Nara Singh membangunnya kembali pada 1844, dan pasukan Inggris menghancurkannya dengan tembakan artileri pada 20 Juli 1891. Pemerintah Manipur mengakui Kangla Sha sebagai lambang negara bagian pada 1980 dan membangun kembali patungnya pada 2006.
long_description.en: According to Wikipedia, Chourjit Singh built two statues in 1804, and Burmese forces demolished them during the Chahi Taret Khuntakpa (1819-1826). King Nara Singh reconstructed them in 1844, and British forces destroyed them with artillery fire on 20 July 1891. The government of Manipur recognised Kangla Sha as the state emblem in 1980 and reconstructed the statues in 2006.

long_description.id: Pada 18 Juni 2021 batang Kaba Khanba pada patung itu dilepas oleh Pemerintah Manipur karena dianggap menyakiti Kangla Sha; langkah ini dikritik oleh RK Nimai.
long_description.en: On 18 June 2021 the Kaba Khanba rods of the statues were removed by the Government of Manipur because they were thought to pain Kangla Sha; the step was criticised by RK Nimai.

short_description.id: Kaupe adalah roh jahat dalam mitologi Hawaii yang digambarkan sebagai pria raksasa berkepala anjing, pemakan manusia, yang pernah menguasai Nu'uanu Valley.
short_description.en: Kaupe is a malevolent spirit in Hawaiian mythology described as an enormous man with a canine head, a man-eater who once ruled Nu'uanu Valley.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Hawaii, Kaupe adalah roh jahat yang memanggil orang pada malam hari untuk memikat mereka menuju kematian, dan konon pernah menguasai Nu'uanu Valley. Selama masa kekuasaannya Kaupe memakan orang di Oahu, lalu di Maui. Menurut mitologi, ia tampak sebagai pria raksasa berkepala anjing dan bercakar tajam.
long_description.en: In Hawaiian mythology Kaupe is a malevolent spirit who calls to people at night to draw them to their deaths, and legend says he once ruled Nu'uanu Valley. While he reigned he ate people on Oahu and then Maui. Myth shows him as a huge man with a dog's head and sharp claws.

long_description.id: Kaupe dianggap "hantu pemanggil" karena ia memanggil korbannya, dengan menirukan suara banyak orang yang terluka atau sekarat. Meski dikatakan berasal dari Nuuanu Valley, ia lebih sering ditemui di bawah Kipapa Bridge.
long_description.en: Kaupe is often thought of as a "calling ghost" since he calls out to his victims, imitating the sounds of many wounded or dying people. Though said to come from Nuuanu Valley, he is more often met beneath Kipapa Bridge.

long_description.id: Beckwith menggambarkan Kaupe sebagai manusia-anjing kanibal yang menggulingkan pemerintahan Ka-hanai-a-ke-akua dan memerintah negeri dari Nu'uanu sampai ke laut. Ia tinggal di Lihue di Oahu, tidak pernah menyerang kepala suku tinggi, tetapi memakan sebagian penduduk Oahu dan Maui, dan membawa putra seorang kepala suku dari Hawaii untuk dikorbankan. Sang ayah mempelajari doa untuk membunuh musuh dan mengalahkan Kaupe di Hawaii.
long_description.en: Beckwith describes Kaupe as a cannibal dog-man who overthrew the government of Ka-hanai-a-ke-akua and ruled the land from Nu'uanu to the sea. He lives at Lihue on Oahu, never attacks a high chief but eats some of the people of Oahu and Maui, and brings back a chief's son from Hawaii to be sacrificed. The father learns a prayer for killing an enemy and defeats Kaupe on Hawaii.

long_description.id: Sebagai dewa hantu yang beristirahat di awan di atas pegunungan Koolau di Oahu, tubuh roh Kaupe kini dikacaukan dengan legenda makhluk mirip anjing bernama Poki.
long_description.en: As a ghost god lying in the clouds over the Koolau range on Oahu, Kaupe's spirit form is now mixed up with legends of a dog-like creature called Poki.

claims.quote: In Hawaiian mythology, Kaupe is a malevolent spirit that calls out to people at night to lure them to their deaths. According to legend, he used to rule Nu'uanu Valley.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Hawaii, Kaupe adalah roh jahat yang memanggil orang di malam hari menuju kematian dan pernah menguasai Nu'uanu Valley.
statement.en: In Hawaiian mythology, Kaupe is a malevolent spirit calling out to lure victims to death, formerly ruling Nu'uanu Valley.

claims.quote: During his reign, Kaupe ate people on Oahu, then Maui.

statement.id: Selama masa kekuasaannya, Kaupe memakan manusia di Oahu lalu di Maui.
statement.en: During his reign, Kaupe ate people on Oahu and Maui.

claims.quote: According to mythology, Kaupe appears as an enormous man with a canine head and sharp claws.

statement.id: Kaupe berwujud pria raksasa dengan kepala anjing dan cakar-cakar tajam.
statement.en: Kaupe appears as an enormous man with a canine head and sharp claws.

claims.quote: Though he is said to originally be from Nuuanu Valley, he is more often encountered under Kipapa Bridge.

statement.id: Meskipun berasal dari Lembah Nuuanu, ia kerap ditemui di bawah Jembatan Kipapa.
statement.en: Though from Nuuanu Valley, he is often encountered under Kipapa Bridge.

claims.quote: Kaupe is often considered a "calling ghost" because he calls to his victims rather than searching them out or coming across them by coincidence. His technique is to mimic the sound of numerous wounded or dying people.

statement.id: Kaupe disebut hantu pemanggil karena menirukan suara rintihan orang terluka atau sekarat untuk memikat mangsanya.
statement.en: Kaupe is considered a calling ghost because he mimics the sound of wounded or dying people to lure victims.

claims.quote: Among dog-men represented as overthrowing the chief of a district and terrorizing the country, the most famous is the cannibal dog-man Kaupe who overthrew the government of Ka-hanai-a-ke-akua (Reared by the gods) and ruled the land from Nu'uanu to the sea.

statement.id: Di antara manusia-anjing yang digambarkan menggulingkan kepala suatu distrik dan meneror negeri, yang paling terkenal ialah manusia-anjing kanibal Kaupe, yang menggulingkan pemerintahan Ka-hanai-a-ke-akua dan memerintah negeri dari Nu'uanu sampai ke laut.
statement.en: Among dog-men represented as overthrowing the chief of a district and terrorizing the country, the most famous is the cannibal dog-man Kaupe, who overthrew the government of Ka-hanai-a-ke-akua and ruled the land from Nu'uanu to the sea.

claims.quote: Kaupe lives at Lihue on Oahu. He never attacks a high chief but eats some of the people both of Oahu and Maui. At last he crosses over to Hawaii and brings back a chief's son to sacrifice in the heiau at Lihue.

statement.id: Kaupe tinggal di Lihue di Oahu; ia tidak pernah menyerang kepala suku tinggi tetapi memakan sebagian penduduk Oahu dan Maui, lalu menyeberang ke Hawaii dan membawa pulang putra seorang kepala suku untuk dikorbankan di heiau di Lihue.
statement.en: Kaupe lives at Lihue on Oahu; he never attacks a high chief but eats some of the people both of Oahu and Maui, then crosses over to Hawaii and brings back a chief's son to sacrifice in the heiau at Lihue.

claims.quote: The prayer unfastens the boy's fetters and father and son flee and hide under a rock at Moanalua while Kaupe goes on to look for them on Hawaii. The father learns the prayer for killing an enemy, and overcomes Kaupe on Hawaii.

statement.id: Doa itu membuka belenggu sang anak, ayah dan anak melarikan diri dan bersembunyi di bawah batu di Moanalua sementara Kaupe mencari mereka di Hawaii; sang ayah mempelajari doa untuk membunuh musuh dan mengalahkan Kaupe di Hawaii.
statement.en: The prayer unfastens the boy's fetters, and father and son flee and hide under a rock at Moanalua while Kaupe goes on to look for them on Hawaii; the father learns the prayer for killing an enemy and overcomes Kaupe on Hawaii.

claims.quote: As a ghost god resting in the clouds stretched over the mountaintops of the Koolau range on Oahu, Kaupe's spirit body is today confused with legends of a dog-like creature called Poki, spotted or brindled in color and very long in body, who guards a certain section outside Honolulu

statement.id: Sebagai dewa hantu yang beristirahat di awan di atas puncak-puncak pegunungan Koolau di Oahu, tubuh roh Kaupe kini dikacaukan dengan legenda makhluk mirip anjing bernama Poki, berbintik atau belang dan sangat panjang tubuhnya, yang menjaga suatu bagian di luar Honolulu.
statement.en: As a ghost god resting in the clouds stretched over the mountaintops of the Koolau range on Oahu, Kaupe's spirit body is today confused with legends of a dog-like creature called Poki, spotted or brindled in color and very long in body, who guards a certain section outside Honolulu.

long_description.id: Kisah itu menyebut ia meniru tangisan bayi untuk menarik orang yang lewat. Cerita belakangan menyebut leluconnya dapat berakhir dengan orang tenggelam. Satu tafsir peneliti menganggap gambar itu sebagai permainan kata, bukan makhluk yang tercatat dalam tradisi rakyat.

short_description.id: Kayberen adalah roh baik hati dalam kepercayaan orang Kirgiz yang tinggal di pegunungan, melindungi hewan pemamah biak, dan dimintai bantuan oleh pemburu serta orang yang terancam bahaya di gunung.
short_description.en: Kayberen are benevolent spirits in Kyrgyz belief who live in the mountains, protect ruminant animals and are called upon by hunters and by people facing danger in the mountains.

long_description.id: Orang Kirgiz menggolongkan Kayberen sebagai roh baik hati yang menetap di gunung dan menjaga hewan pemamah biak. Roh-roh ini membuat ternak dan satwa bertambah banyak, tetapi bila marah mereka bisa membinasakan hewan. Karena itu, sebelum berburu orang memohon pertolongan mereka agar perburuan beruntung.
long_description.en: The Kyrgyz class the Kayberen as kindly spirits who dwell in the mountains and look after cud-chewing animals. These spirits let herds and game grow in number, yet when angered they can wipe animals out. For that reason people seek their help before a hunt so that it will go well.

long_description.id: Kayberen juga menjadi iye, yaitu pemilik gaib, dari gunung dan bebatuan tempat mereka tinggal, dan orang yang menghadapi bahaya di gunung meminta bantuan mereka. Kamus kedua mencatat bahwa dalam kepercayaan rakyat Kirgiz mereka adalah orang-orang suci tak kasatmata yang disebut juga Yitik Eren atau Kayıp Eren. Kepercayaan ini bercampur dengan sosok Çiltan, empat puluh penjaga gunung yang juga melindungi hewan.
long_description.en: The Kayberen are also the iye, the spirit owners, of the mountains and rocks they inhabit, and those in danger in the mountains call on them for help. The second source notes that in Kyrgyz folk belief they are unseen holy ones, also known as Yitik Eren or Kayıp Eren. The belief has blended with the Çiltan, forty mountain guardians who likewise protect animals.

long_description.id: Artikel pertama mengaitkan kepercayaan Kayberen dengan kultus leluhur dan mencatat bahwa namanya dikenal di banyak bangsa Turk. Di kalangan orang Turk Anatolia, kayberen dipahami sebagai roh para wali yang mengambil rupa manusia, dan penduduk setempat menyembelih kurban untuk mereka setiap musim panas dan musim gugur.
long_description.en: The first article ties the Kayberen belief to the ancestor cult and notes that the name is known among many Turkic peoples. Among the Anatolian Turks, the kayberen are understood as the spirits of saints in human guise, and local people offer sacrifices to them every summer and autumn.

long_description.id: Sebuah legenda menceritakan pasangan tua yang lama mendambakan anak. Ketika mereka sudah renta, Tuhan memberi mereka empat puluh anak, yang lalu ditinggalkan di gunung karena tak sanggup diasuh. Kayberen datang membesarkan anak-anak itu, dan setelah dewasa mereka berubah menjadi pelindung yang tidak terlihat oleh manusia.
long_description.en: A legend tells of an old couple who had long wished for children. When they were already frail, God granted them forty children, whom they left on a mountain because they could not care for them. The Kayberen came and raised the children, who on growing up turned into protectors unseen by people.

who.en: Kayberen are animal-protecting spirits who live in the mountains.

origin.id: Mereka berasal dari kepercayaan orang Kirgiz, dan namanya dikenal di banyak bangsa Turk.
origin.en: They come from Kyrgyz belief, and the name is known among many Turkic peoples.

role.id: Mereka menjaga dan memperbanyak hewan serta menolong orang yang terancam bahaya di gunung.
role.en: They guard and multiply animals and help people in danger in the mountains.

famous_for.id: Mereka dikenal dalam legenda empat puluh anak yang mereka besarkan menjadi pelindung tak terlihat.
famous_for.en: They are known from the legend of forty children they raised to become unseen protectors.

did_you_know.en: The name Kayberen is formed from kayıp, meaning invisible, and eren, meaning holy.

role.en: Foster carers of the abandoned children

summary.en: An old couple were given forty children by God and left them on a mountain; the Kayberen raised them until they became unseen protectors.

note.en: The forty Çiltan also live in the mountains and protect animals; beliefs about the two have blended.

claims.quote: Kayberen, Kırgızlar'ın iyiliksever ruhlar arasına dahil ettikleri ve ... dağlarda yaşarlar ... ve geviş getiren hayvanları korurlar.

statement.id: Kayberen adalah roh yang digolongkan orang Kirgiz ke dalam roh-roh baik hati; mereka tinggal di pegunungan (dağlarda yaşarlar) dan melindungi hewan pemamah biak (geviş getiren hayvanları korurlar).
statement.en: Kayberen are spirits whom the Kyrgyz count among the benevolent spirits; they live in the mountains (dağlarda yaşarlar) and protect ruminant animals (geviş getiren hayvanları korurlar).

claims.quote: Kırgızlar'ın inancına göre bu ruhlar, hayvanların artıp çoğalmasını sağlar. Ancak kızdıkları zaman da hayvanları telef edebilir.

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan orang Kirgiz (Kırgızlar), roh-roh ini membuat hewan bertambah dan berkembang biak (artıp çoğalmasını), tetapi ketika marah (kızdıkları zaman) mereka juga dapat membinasakan hewan (telef edebilir).
statement.en: According to the belief of the Kyrgyz (Kırgızlar), these spirits make animals increase and multiply (artıp çoğalmasını), but when angry (kızdıkları zaman) they can also destroy animals (telef edebilir).

claims.quote: Bunun için de ava çıkmadan önce, uğurlu geçmesi için

statement.id: Karena itu sebelum berburu (ava çıkmadan önce), orang meminta bantuan kepada kayberen agar perburuan membawa keberuntungan (uğurlu geçmesi için).
statement.en: Therefore before going hunting (ava çıkmadan önce), people ask the kayberen for help so that it goes auspiciously (uğurlu geçmesi için).

claims.quote: Dağlarda, taşlarda yaşayan ve hayvanları koruyan bu ruhlar aynı zamanda yaşadıkları yerin iyesidirler.

statement.id: Roh-roh yang tinggal di gunung dan bebatuan serta melindungi hewan ini sekaligus adalah iye (pemilik, iyesidirler) tempat tinggal mereka.
statement.en: These spirits, living in mountains and rocks and protecting animals, are at the same time the iye (owners, iyesidirler) of the places they inhabit.

claims.quote: Çiltanlar (Kırklar)da Kayberenler gibi dağda yaşayıp hayvanları korurlardı. Onların sayısı 40 olduğu için kırk çiltan denilirdi.

statement.id: Çiltan (Kırklar) juga tinggal di gunung dan melindungi hewan seperti Kayberen; karena jumlahnya 40, mereka disebut kırk çiltan (empat puluh çiltan).
statement.en: The Çiltan (Kırklar) also lived in the mountains and protected animals like the Kayberen; because they numbered 40 they were called kırk çiltan (the forty çiltan).

claims.quote: Kayberen inancı ata kültüyle bağlıdır. Onun adına, Türk halklarının birçoğunda rastlanır.

statement.id: Kepercayaan Kayberen terkait dengan kultus leluhur (ata kültü), dan namanya dijumpai di banyak bangsa Turk (Türk halklarının).
statement.en: The Kayberen belief is linked to the ancestor cult (ata kültü), and its name is found among many Turkic peoples (Türk halklarının).

claims.quote: Anadolu Türkleri'nde "kayb erenleri" şeklinde rastlanır ve eski inanışların bir izi gibi, evliyalar hakkında görüşlerden kaynaklanan bir anlayışı ifade eder. Bu inanışa göre "kayberenler", evliyaların insan kılığına girmiş ruhlarıdır.

statement.id: Di kalangan orang Turk Anatolia (Anadolu Türkleri) dikenal kayb erenleri; menurut kepercayaan ini, kayberen adalah roh para wali (evliyaların) yang mengambil rupa manusia (insan kılığına girmiş).
statement.en: Among the Anatolian Turks (Anadolu Türkleri) they are known as kayb erenleri; according to this belief the kayberen are the spirits of saints (evliyaların) who have taken human guise (insan kılığına girmiş).

claims.quote: Yerli halk tarafından her yılın yazı ve sonbaharında

statement.id: Penduduk setempat (yerli halk) menyembelih kurban untuk kayberen setiap musim panas dan musim gugur (yazı ve sonbaharında).
statement.en: The local people (yerli halk) slaughter sacrifices for the kayberen every summer and autumn (yazı ve sonbaharında).

claims.quote: Kayberenler gelip onları yedirir, içirir ve büyütür. Bu kırk çocuk büyüdükten sonra, insanların gözüne görünmeyen koruyuculara dönüşürler.

statement.id: Dalam legenda, Kayberen datang memberi makan, minum, dan membesarkan anak-anak itu (yedirir, içirir ve büyütür); setelah dewasa, keempat puluh anak itu (kırk çocuk) menjadi pelindung yang tak terlihat manusia (gözüne görünmeyen koruyuculara).
statement.en: In the legend, the Kayberen come and feed, water and raise the children (yedirir, içirir ve büyütür); once grown, these forty children (kırk çocuk) become protectors invisible to human eyes (gözüne görünmeyen koruyuculara).

claims.quote: Bir karı kocanın hiç çocukları yoktu. Ömürleri boyunca çocuk sahibi olmak için Tanrı'ya yalvardılar.

statement.id: Sepasang suami istri (karı koca) tidak punya anak dan sepanjang hidup memohon kepada Tuhan (Tanrı) agar diberi anak.
statement.en: A husband and wife (karı koca) had no children and all their lives begged God (Tanrı) for a child.

statement.en: According to Kyrgyz (Kırgızların) folk beliefs, there are holy ones invisible to the eye (gözle görülemeyen) who live in remote mountains, called Yitik Eren (Yitkin Eren, İtkin Eren).

statement.id: Orang-orang suci yang juga disebut Kayıp Eren (Kayberen, Kaybaran) itu melindungi hewan (hayvanları korurlar), menjadi iye atau pemilik tempat tinggalnya, dan orang yang menghadapi bahaya di gunung meminta bantuan mereka (yardım isterler).
statement.en: These holy ones, also called Kayıp Eren (Kayberen, Kaybaran), protect animals (hayvanları korurlar), are the iye or owners of the places they live in, and those who meet danger in the mountains ask them for help (yardım isterler).

short_description.id: Raja Goldemar adalah kurcaci atau kobold dari mitologi dan folklor Jermanik, yang pada Abad Pertengahan dianggap raja para kurcaci.
short_description.en: King Goldemar is a dwarf or kobold of Germanic myth and folklore, regarded by the Middle Ages as king of the dwarfs.

long_description.id: Raja Goldemar (juga Goldmar, Vollmar, Volmar) adalah kurcaci atau kobold dari mitologi dan folklor Jermanik; pada Abad Pertengahan ia telah menjadi raja kurcaci dalam kepercayaan Jerman. Penggalan puisi epik Goldemar karya Albrecht von Kemenaten mengisahkan pertemuan Dietrich dengan raja kurcaci itu, dan ia juga muncul dalam "Der junge König und die Schäferin" karya Ludwig Uhland. Saudara-saudaranya, Alberich (Elberich) dan Elbegast, tampil dalam puisi lain.
long_description.en: King Goldemar (also Goldmar, Vollmar, Volmar) is a dwarf or kobold of Germanic myth and folklore who by the Middle Ages was held in German belief to rule the dwarfs. Surviving fragments of Albrecht von Kemenaten's epic Goldemar describe Dietrich meeting the dwarf king, and he also figures in Ludwig Uhland's 'Der junge König und die Schäferin'. His brothers Alberich (Elberich) and Elbegast appear in other poems.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda yang dicatat Thomas Keightley pada 1850, Goldemar adalah kobold, roh rumah, yang tinggal bersama Neveling von Hardenberg di Kastel Hardenstein di tepi Sungai Ruhr. Ia pandai bermain harpa, gemar berjudi dadu, membawa keberuntungan, dan tak mau dilihat meski boleh diraba. Setelah tiga tahun, seorang yang penasaran menaburkan abu untuk melihat jejaknya; Goldemar mencincang orang itu, memasak dan memakannya, lalu pergi sambil meninggalkan pesan bahwa rumah itu akan sial sebagaimana dulu beruntung.
long_description.en: In a legend Thomas Keightley recorded in 1850, Goldemar was a kobold, a household spirit, living with Neveling von Hardenberg at Castle Hardenstein by the River Ruhr. He played the harp well, liked dice, brought luck to the house, and would be felt but never seen. After three years a curious man scattered ashes to find his footprints; Goldemar hacked him apart, cooked and ate him, and departed, leaving word that the house would now be as unlucky as it had been lucky.

short_description.id: Kitovras adalah makhluk setengah manusia setengah kuda dalam apokrif Rusia, saudara sekaligus saingan Raja Salomo yang terkenal karena kebijaksanaannya.
short_description.en: Kitovras is a half-man, half-horse being of Russian apocrypha, brother and rival of King Solomon, famed for his wisdom.

long_description.id: Kitovras adalah makhluk setengah manusia setengah kuda, tokoh dalam kisah-kisah apokrif. Namanya bisa berarti monster secara umum atau nama diri, dan ia digambarkan sebagai monster kentaur, kadang bersayap. Raja Salomo dan Kitovras sudah digambarkan pada panel Pintu Vasilievsky (1335–1336) di Katedral Santa Sofia, Novgorod.
long_description.en: Kitovras is a half-man, half-horse being, a hero of apocryphal tales. The name could mean a monster in general or be a proper name, and he was depicted as a centaur-like monster, sometimes winged. King Solomon and Kitovras already appear on a panel of the Vasilievsky Gates (1335–1336) of St Sophia's Cathedral in Novgorod.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah-kisah tentang Salomo, Kitovras kadang menjadi saudara dan rekannya, kadang musuh dan saingannya. Ia makhluk yang tahu masa depan: ketika ditangkap Salomo, ia membuatnya takjub dengan kebijaksanaannya. Dalam kisah kemudian ia memerintah kota Lukorye sebagai raja manusia pada siang hari dan raja hewan pada malam hari, dan kadang menculik istri Salomo lalu tewas bertarung dengannya.
long_description.en: In the tales of Solomon, Kitovras is sometimes his brother and companion, sometimes his enemy and rival. He is a prophetic being: captured by Solomon, he astonishes him with his wisdom. In later tales he rules the city of Lukorye, king of men by day and of beasts by night, and sometimes abducts Solomon's wife and dies fighting him.

long_description.id: Menurut sebuah ensiklopedia Rusia lama, nama Kitovras dianggap berasal dari kata Yunani untuk kentaur. Dalam kisah-kisah Yahudi yang sepadan dengan apokrif Rusia tentang Salomo dan Kitovras, yang tampil menggantikannya adalah iblis Asmodeus.
long_description.en: According to an old Russian encyclopedia, the name Kitovras is held to derive from the Greek word for centaur. In the Jewish tales corresponding to the Russian apocrypha about Solomon and Kitovras, the demon Asmodeus appears in his place.

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
